Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 68, verses 1–4:

It is Meccan. It has fifty-two verses, three hundred words, and one thousand two hundred and fifty-six letters.

It was related to us by Muhammad ibn al-Qayyim, who said: Muhammad ibn Taha related to us, who said: Ibrahim ibn Shurayk related to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah related to us, who said: Salam ibn Sulaym related to us, who said: Harun ibn Kathir related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his son, from Abu Umamah ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the surah *Nun, wal-Qalam* (68), Allah will grant him the reward of those whose character Allah has made good." [1] [[Majma' al-Bayan: 10/82.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

**Nun.** The reciters differed concerning it. Some made its *nun* clear (*izhar*), while others concealed it (*ikhfa'*). Ibn Abbas read *Ni* with a kasra on the nun, on the assumption that a particle of oath is elided before it. Isa ibn Umar read it with a fatha, on the assumption that a verb such as *a'nni* (or similar) is elided before it.

The commentators differed about its meaning. Mujahid, Muqatil, Murrah al-Hamdani, Ata al-Khurasani, al-Suddi and al-Kalbi said:

It is the fish (*hut*) that carries the earth. This is the report of Abu Zabyan from Ibn Abbas, who said: The first thing Allah created was the pen, and it ran by what was to be until the Day of Resurrection. Then He raised it and created water, and from it He created the heavens. Then He created the *nun* and spread the earth upon the back of the *nun*. The *nun* moved, and the earth shook, so it was steadied with mountains, for the mountains boast over the earth. Then Ibn Abbas recited: *Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe* [68:1].

They differed about its name. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: *Yahmut*. Abu al-Yaqzan, al-Waqidi and Abu Ka'b said: *Lawsa*.

Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: *Yalhut*. And the rajiz said:

*What is it with you, that I see you all silent?*
*By Allah, my Lord is the Creator of the Yalhut.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/224, where it reads "al-Bahmut".]]

The narrators said: When Allah, exalted is He, created the earth and split it open, He sent from beneath the Throne an angel. He descended to the earth until he entered beneath the seven earths, and placed them upon his shoulder: one of his hands in the east and the other in the west, outstretched and grasping the seven earths, until he held them firm. But there was no place of rest for his foot. So Allah, exalted is He, sent down from Paradise (*al-Firdaws*) a bull with forty thousand horns and forty thousand legs, and placed the resting place of the angel's foot upon its hump. But his feet did not settle. So Allah caused a red ruby to descend from the highest rank of Paradise, whose thickness was a five-hundred-year journey, and placed it between the bull's hump and its ear, and his feet settled upon it. The horns of that bull extend out to the edges of the earth, and its nostrils are in the sea. It breathes out one breath each day; when it breathes out, the sea rises, and when it draws in its breath, the sea recedes. But the bull's hooves had no place of rest. So Allah created a green rock, as thick as the seven heavens and the seven earths, and the bull's hooves settled upon it. This is the rock of which Luqman said to his son: *"It would be in a rock"* (31:16). But the rock had no place of rest, so Allah created a *nun*, which is the great fish, and placed the rock upon its back and along its side. The fish is upon the sea, the sea is upon the wind, the wind is upon the power, and the weight of the whole world with what is upon it rests on two letters from the Book of Allah, exalted is He. The Almighty said to it: "Be," and it was.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Iblis penetrated to the fish upon whose back the whole earth rests, and whispered to it, saying: "Do you know what is upon your back, O Luwtiya, of nations, animals, trees, mountains and other things? If you shook them off, you would cast them all from your back." He said: Luwtiya resolved to do that, but Allah sent a creature which entered its nostril and reached its brain. The fish cried out to Allah because of it, so He permitted it, and it came out. Ka'b said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, it looks at it and it looks at it; if it intends anything of that, it returns to what it was.

Some of them said: It is the last letter of *al-Rahman* (the Most Gracious). This is the report of Ikrimah from Ibn Abbas, who said: *Alif Lam Mim*? No: *Ra, Ha, Mim, Nun*, the letters of *al-Rahman*, blessed and exalted is He, separated.

Al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: The *nun* is the inkwell (*diwah*). This is the report of Thabit al-Yamani from Ibn Abbas. The poet said concerning it:

*When longing drives me toward them,*
*the nun casts down tears that flow like pearls.*

Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah said: It is a tablet of light, and he traced it back to the Prophet (ﷺ). [[See Tafsir al-Tabari: 29/21.]]

Ibn Zayd said: It is an oath which Allah, exalted is He, swore by. Ibn Kaysan said: It is the opening of the surah. Ata said: It is the opening letter of His name *Nur* (Light), *Nasir* (Helper) and *Nasir* (Victor). [[In Tafsir al-Qurtubi (15/289): The *ha'* is the opening of His names *Hamid* (Praiseworthy), *Hannan* (Compassionate), *Halim* (Forbearing) and *Hakim* (Wise), and the *mim* is the opening of His names *Malik* (King), *Majid* (Glorious), *Mannan* (Bestower), *Mutakabbir* (Majestic) and *Musawwir* (Fashioner).]] Al-Qurazi said: Allah swore by His support of the believers, as is shown by His saying: *It was ever a duty upon Us to help the believers* (30:47).

Ja'far al-Sadiq said: It is a river in Paradise. [[Zad al-Masir: 8/65.]]

***Wal-Qalam* (By the pen).** It is the pen with which the Reminder (*al-Dhikr*) was written. It is a pen of light, which lies between the heaven and the earth. It is said: When Allah created the pen, and it was the first thing He created, He looked at it, and it split into two halves. Then He said: "Run." It said: "O Lord, with what shall I run?" He said: "With what is to be until the Day of Resurrection." So it ran upon the Preserved Tablet by that.

Ata said: I asked al-Walid ibn Ubadah ibn al-Samit: What was the will of your father when death came to him? He said: He called me and said: "My son, fear Allah, and know that you will not fear Allah, nor will you attain knowledge, until you believe in Allah alone, and in the decree, its good and its evil. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The first thing Allah created was the pen. He said to it: Write. It said: O Lord, what shall I write? He said: Write the knowledge [[In the source: the decree.]].' So the pen ran at that hour, with what is to be forever." [2] [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 9/3.]]

It is related that Ibn al-Zayyat entered upon one of the caliphs and found him sorrowful. He said to him: "Refresh me, O Ibn al-Zayyat." So he composed:

*O Allah, the decree is Yours, and the decree prevails,*
*and the writing was on the tablet.*
*Wait for relief and its causes,*
*for despair is the worst thing you have while in relief.* [[Sharh Nahj al-Balaghah by Ibn Abi al-Hadid: 5/165.]]

Did he mean by the pen the writing and script, by which Allah bestowed favour upon His servants when He taught them? That is as He said: *He taught by the pen* (96:4).

The sages and eloquent speakers have greatly described the pen and its benefit. So why would one wish to leave this book without reflecting upon its gems?

Ibn Haytham said: From the majesty of the pen is that no book was written for Allah except with it, and therefore Allah swore by it. It was said: Pens are the mounts of the intelligent and the messengers of the noble.

It was said: The pen is the greatest injustice. It was said: Eloquence is of two kinds: eloquence of the tongue and eloquence of the fingers. The excellence of the eloquence of the fingers is that what the pens fix remains through the days, while the eloquence of the tongue is effaced by the years.

One of the sages said: The affairs of religion and of the world are sustained by two things: the pen and the sword, and the sword is under the banner of knowledge. Their poet said concerning this:

*If the pen serves the sword, before which the necks have bowed*
*and before whose wariness the nations have submitted,*
*then death, and death cannot be overcome by anything,*
*it has always followed what the pen has run by.*

*Thus Allah decreed for the pens, since they were created,*
*that the swords have been their servants since they were sharpened.* [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/85.]]

And al-Sanawbari said:

*A pen of weak, hollow reed*
*is more effective than a long, spear-like javelin.*
*And of blades, when they appear, I meet them,*
*and of the Indian sword polished and burnished.* [[al-Murhaf: a thin blade (Lisan al-Arab 12/99).]]

*And more daring than the lion*
*that scorches hearts when it appears on the battlefield.*

Abu al-Qayyim al-Sadusi recited, saying: Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi recited to me, saying: Ibn Safwan recited to me, a verse of Abu Tammam on its meaning:

*A blow from a writer with his eloquence*
*is more effective and more far-reaching than a keen sword.*
*People, when they resolve on hostility toward an envier,*
*shed blood with the points of pens.*

And al-Buhturi said:

*People, when they sharpen pens in anger,*
*then draw from them the water of desires,*
*gain by them over their enemies, though they are many,*
*what they could not gain by the Mashrafi swords.*

Another said:

*The sword, in anger, its polish shines,*
*but it is no more effective against calamities than its pen.*

And Ibn al-Rumi said:

*In his hand is a pen, and you need no more than a pen,*
*a sufficient arrow, and enough of a hand wrapped in it.*
*By it he erases and affirms the sustenance of servants,*
*so destinies are nothing but what he writes and erases.*

He said: And one of them recited in its description:

*A mute who speaks with decisive words,*
*whose body is silent and hollow,*
*all of him speaks within its sheath,*
*and by its silence its speech is known.*

And another in its description:

*Its bones are thin after its head was full,*
*it wastes and its enemy grows strong when it is cut.*
*It is dark at the height of day, its tongue*
*understands one who speaks what is not heard.*

*Its nourishment, and the trees that grow in its poverty,*
*when they are cut, the mounts of the fingers are bewildered.*
*For it the weeping of lovers, and their color,*
*except that they weep black tears.*

Another:

*This is the first verse for the two following verses:*
*It is attached, its edge is wholly single,*
*it erases some creation or death,*
*by its walking it is a living serpent, and by its color a spirit,*
*and the crime of a lover and the characteristics of good things.* [[So it is in the manuscript.]]

His saying: *And what they inscribe* (68:1): they write. It may mean: "and what writes them," meaning the scribes (*al-Safarah*). It was said: They are the plural of *al-katabah* (scribes).

*You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman* (68:2) means: you are not a madman, since Allah has favoured you with prophethood. It was said: by the protection of your Lord. It was said: It is like saying, "You are not a madman, praise be to Allah." It was said: The meaning is "You are not a madman, and the blessing belongs to your Lord," like their saying: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You," meaning "and praise belongs to You." Labid said:

*I was left alone in the world, having lost my tribe,*
*and a beneficial neighbour at Arbad departed from me.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/226, concerning the verse.]]

That is: "and he is Arbad."

Al-Nabighah said:

*They did not deprive themselves of the goodness of food, and their mother*
*was overflowed upon you by a rain-cloud, a male lightning-bringer.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/226.]]

That is: "and he is the rain-bringer."

*And indeed for you is a reward never cut off* (68:3): uncut and not diminished, from their saying: "a rope that is *manin*" when it is not strong.

*And indeed you are upon a magnificent character* (68:4). Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: a magnificent religion. Al-Hasan said: his character was the manners of the Qur'an. Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her), when she was asked about the character of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), said: "His character was the Qur'an."

Qatadah said: It is what he would enact of Allah's command and refrain from of Allah's prohibition. Junayd said: His character was called magnificent because he had no aspiration other than Allah.

Al-Wasiti said: Because he gave both worlds in exchange for the Truth. It was said: Because he associated with people through his character and detached from them in his heart, so his outward was with creation and his inward was with the Real. One of the sages advised a man, saying: "Hold to the truth with creation, and to sincerity with the Real."

It was said: Because he dedicated the world to Allah, exalted is He, as Allah commanded him by His saying: *Take what is easy of forgiveness* (7:199), and the rest of the verse. It was said: His character was made magnificent because He made the colours small in his eyes, so that he might know their Creator.

It was said: His character was called magnificent because the noble qualities were gathered in him, as is indicated by what

It was related to us by Abu al-Qayyim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad the exegete, who said: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Saffar related to us, who said: Ibn Abi al-Rima related to us, who said: al-Darawardi related to us, from Ibn Ajlan, from al-Qa'qa', from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was sent only to perfect noble character." [3] [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 10/192.]]

And he said: "My Lord disciplined me, and He made my discipline excellent." [4] [[al-Jami' al-Saghir: 1/51.]]

It was related to us by Abu Amr Ahmad ibn Abi al-Farabi, grandfather of Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm, who said: Ibn Abd al-Hakam related to us, who said: My father and Shu'ayb related to us, and al-Layth related to us, from Umar ibn Abi Amr, from al-Muttalib ibn Abd Allah, from Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Indeed the believer attains by his good character the rank of one who stands in prayer at night and fasts by day." [5] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/64.]]

He said: And Ahmad ibn Abi al-Farabi related to us, who said: Mansur ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ayyub al-Razi related to us, who said: Abu al-Walid related to us, who said: Shu'bah related to us, from al-Qasim and Abu Qurrah, who said: I heard Ata al-Kaykharani, from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Nothing is heavier in the scale than good character." [6] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/446.]]

It was related to us by Ahmad ibn al-Sari al-Arudi in Darb al-Hajib, who said: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far al-Amani related to us, who said: Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Amir al-Ta'i related to us, who said: My father related to me, who said: Ali ibn Musa al-Rida related to us, who said: My father Musa ibn Ja'far related to us, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah said:

"Hold to good character, for good character is surely in Paradise, and beware of bad character, for bad character is surely in the Fire." [7] [[Majma' al-Bayan: 10/87.]]

It was related to us by Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanbah related to us, who said: Sam'an related to us, from Ibn al-Jarud, who said: Salih related to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Abu Uthman al-Yahri, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"The most beloved of you to Allah [[In the source: to me.]] are those of you with the best character, those who are gentle and easy to approach, who love and are loved. And the most hated of you to Allah are those who go about with tale-bearing, who sow discord between friends [[In the source: the beloved.]], who seek out the faults of the innocent." [8] [[al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 7/350.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 68, verses 1–4:

It was related to us by Muhammad ibn al-Qayyim, who said: Muhammad ibn Taha related to us, who said: Ibrahim ibn Shurayk related to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah related to us, who said: Salam ibn Sulaym related to us, who said: Harun ibn Kathir related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his son, from Abu Umamah ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the surah *Nun, wal-Qalam* (68), Allah will grant him the reward of those whose character Allah has made good." [1] [[Majma' al-Bayan: 10/82.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

**Nun.** The reciters differed concerning it. Some made its *nun* clear (*izhar*), while others concealed it (*ikhfa'*). Ibn Abbas read *Ni* with a kasra on the nun, on the assumption that a particle of oath is elided before it. The commentators differed about its meaning. Mujahid, Muqatil, Murrah al-Hamdani, Ata al-Khurasani, al-Suddi and al-Kalbi said:

It is the fish (*hut*) that carries the earth. This is the report of Abu Zabyan from Ibn Abbas, who said: The first thing Allah created was the pen, and it ran by what was to be until the Day of Resurrection. Then He raised it and created water, and from it He created the heavens. Then He created the *nun* and spread the earth upon the back of the *nun*. The *nun* moved, and the earth shook, so it was steadied with mountains, for the mountains boast over the earth. Then Ibn Abbas recited: *Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe* [68:1].

They differed about its name. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: *Yahmut*. Abu al-Yaqzan, al-Waqidi and Abu Ka'b said: *Lawsa*.

Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: *Yalhut*. And the rajiz said:

*What is it with you, that I see you all silent?*
*By Allah, my Lord is the Creator of the Yalhut.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/224, where it reads "al-Bahmut".]]

The narrators said: When Allah, exalted is He, created the earth and split it open, He sent from beneath the Throne an angel. He descended to the earth until he entered beneath the seven earths, and placed them upon his shoulder: one of his hands in the east and the other in the west, outstretched and grasping the seven earths, until he held them firm. But there was no place of rest for his foot. So Allah, exalted is He, sent down from Paradise (*al-Firdaws*) a bull with forty thousand horns and forty thousand legs, and placed the resting place of the angel's foot upon its hump. But his feet did not settle. So Allah caused a red ruby to descend from the highest rank of Paradise, whose thickness was a five-hundred-year journey, and placed it between the bull's hump and its ear, and his feet settled upon it. The horns of that bull extend out to the edges of the earth, and its nostrils are in the sea. It breathes out one breath each day; when it breathes out, the sea rises, and when it draws in its breath, the sea recedes. But the bull's hooves had no place of rest. So Allah created a green rock, as thick as the seven heavens and the seven earths, and the bull's hooves settled upon it. This is the rock of which Luqman said to his son: *"It would be in a rock"* (31:16). But the rock had no place of rest, so Allah created a *nun*, which is the great fish, and placed the rock upon its back and along its side. The fish is upon the sea, the sea is upon the wind, the wind is upon the power, and the weight of the whole world with what is upon it rests on two letters from the Book of Allah, exalted is He. The Almighty said to it: "Be," and it was.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Iblis penetrated to the fish upon whose back the whole earth rests, and whispered to it, saying: "Do you know what is upon your back, O Luwtiya, of nations, animals, trees, mountains and other things? If you shook them off, you would cast them all from your back." He said: Luwtiya resolved to do that, but Allah sent a creature which entered its nostril and reached its brain. The fish cried out to Allah because of it, so He permitted it, and it came out. Ka'b said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, it looks at it and it looks at it; if it intends anything of that, it returns to what it was.

Some of them said: It is the last letter of *al-Rahman* (the Most Gracious). This is the report of Ikrimah from Ibn Abbas, who said: *Alif Lam Mim*? No: *Ra, Ha, Mim, Nun*, the letters of *al-Rahman*, blessed and exalted is He, separated.

Al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: The *nun* is the inkwell (*diwah*). This is the report of Thabit al-Yamani from Ibn Abbas. The poet said concerning it:

*When longing drives me toward them,*
*the nun casts down tears that flow like pearls.*

Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah said: It is a tablet of light, and he traced it back to the Prophet (ﷺ). [[See Tafsir al-Tabari: 29/21.]]

Ibn Zayd said: It is an oath which Allah, exalted is He, swore by. Ibn Kaysan said: It is the opening of the surah. Ata said: It is the opening letter of His name *Nur* (Light), *Nasir* (Helper) and *Nasir* (Victor). [[In Tafsir al-Qurtubi (15/289): The *ha'* is the opening of His names *Hamid* (Praiseworthy), *Hannan* (Compassionate), *Halim* (Forbearing) and *Hakim* (Wise), and the *mim* is the opening of His names *Malik* (King), *Majid* (Glorious), *Mannan* (Bestower), *Mutakabbir* (Majestic) and *Musawwir* (Fashioner).]] Al-Qurazi said: Allah swore by His support of the believers, as is shown by His saying: *It was ever a duty upon Us to help the believers* (30:47).

Ja'far al-Sadiq said: It is a river in Paradise. [[Zad al-Masir: 8/65.]]

***Wal-Qalam* (By the pen).** It is the pen with which the Reminder (*al-Dhikr*) was written. It is a pen of light, which lies between the heaven and the earth. It is said: When Allah created the pen, and it was the first thing He created, He looked at it, and it split into two halves. Then He said: "Run." It said: "O Lord, with what shall I run?" He said: "With what is to be until the Day of Resurrection." So it ran upon the Preserved Tablet by that.

Ata said: I asked al-Walid ibn Ubadah ibn al-Samit: What was the will of your father when death came to him? He said: He called me and said: "My son, fear Allah, and know that you will not fear Allah, nor will you attain knowledge, until you believe in Allah alone, and in the decree, its good and its evil. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The first thing Allah created was the pen. He said to it: Write. It said: O Lord, what shall I write? He said: Write the knowledge [[In the source: the decree.]].' So the pen ran at that hour, with what is to be forever." [2] [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 9/3.]]

It is related that Ibn al-Zayyat entered upon one of the caliphs and found him sorrowful. He said to him: "Refresh me, O Ibn al-Zayyat." So he composed:

*O Allah, the decree is Yours, and the decree prevails,*
*and the writing was on the tablet.*
*Wait for relief and its causes,*
*for despair is the worst thing you have while in relief.* [[Sharh Nahj al-Balaghah by Ibn Abi al-Hadid: 5/165.]]

Did he mean by the pen the writing and script, by which Allah bestowed favour upon His servants when He taught them? That is as He said: *He taught by the pen* (96:4).

The sages and eloquent speakers have greatly described the pen and its benefit. So why would one wish to leave this book without reflecting upon its gems?

Ibn Haytham said: From the majesty of the pen is that no book was written for Allah except with it, and therefore Allah swore by it. It was said: Pens are the mounts of the intelligent and the messengers of the noble.

It was said: The pen is the greatest injustice. It was said: Eloquence is of two kinds: eloquence of the tongue and eloquence of the fingers. The excellence of the eloquence of the fingers is that what the pens fix remains through the days, while the eloquence of the tongue is effaced by the years.

One of the sages said: The affairs of religion and of the world are sustained by two things: the pen and the sword, and the sword is under the banner of knowledge. Their poet said concerning this:

*If the pen serves the sword, before which the necks have bowed*
*and before whose wariness the nations have submitted,*
*then death, and death cannot be overcome by anything,*
*it has always followed what the pen has run by.*

*Thus Allah decreed for the pens, since they were created,*
*that the swords have been their servants since they were sharpened.* [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/85.]]

And al-Sanawbari said:

*A pen of weak, hollow reed*
*is more effective than a long, spear-like javelin.*
*And of blades, when they appear, I meet them,*
*and of the Indian sword polished and burnished.* [[al-Murhaf: a thin blade (Lisan al-Arab 12/99).]]

*And more daring than the lion*
*that scorches hearts when it appears on the battlefield.*

Abu al-Qayyim al-Sadusi recited, saying: Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi recited to me, saying: Ibn Safwan recited to me, a verse of Abu Tammam on its meaning:

*A blow from a writer with his eloquence*
*is more effective and more far-reaching than a keen sword.*
*People, when they resolve on hostility toward an envier,*
*shed blood with the points of pens.*

And al-Buhturi said:

*People, when they sharpen pens in anger,*
*then draw from them the water of desires,*
*gain by them over their enemies, though they are many,*
*what they could not gain by the Mashrafi swords.*

Another said:

*The sword, in anger, its polish shines,*
*but it is no more effective against calamities than its pen.*

And Ibn al-Rumi said:

*In his hand is a pen, and you need no more than a pen,*
*a sufficient arrow, and enough of a hand wrapped in it.*
*By it he erases and affirms the sustenance of servants,*
*so destinies are nothing but what he writes and erases.*

He said: And one of them recited in its description:

*A mute who speaks with decisive words,*
*whose body is silent and hollow,*
*all of him speaks within its sheath,*
*and by its silence its speech is known.*

And another in its description:

*Its bones are thin after its head was full,*
*it wastes and its enemy grows strong when it is cut.*
*It is dark at the height of day, its tongue*
*understands one who speaks what is not heard.*

*Its nourishment, and the trees that grow in its poverty,*
*when they are cut, the mounts of the fingers are bewildered.*
*For it the weeping of lovers, and their color,*
*except that they weep black tears.*

Another:

*This is the first verse for the two following verses:*
*It is attached, its edge is wholly single,*
*it erases some creation or death,*
*by its walking it is a living serpent, and by its color a spirit,*
*and the crime of a lover and the characteristics of good things.* [[So it is in the manuscript.]]

His saying: *And what they inscribe* (68:1): they write. It may mean: "and what writes them," meaning the scribes (*al-Safarah*). It was said: They are the plural of *al-katabah* (scribes).

*You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman* (68:2) means: you are not a madman, since Allah has favoured you with prophethood. It was said: by the protection of your Lord. It was said: It is like saying, "You are not a madman, praise be to Allah." It was said: The meaning is "You are not a madman, and the blessing belongs to your Lord," like their saying: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You," meaning "and praise belongs to You." Labid said:

*I was left alone in the world, having lost my tribe,*
*and a beneficial neighbour at Arbad departed from me.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/226, concerning the verse.]]

That is: "and he is Arbad."

Al-Nabighah said:

*They did not deprive themselves of the goodness of food, and their mother*
*was overflowed upon you by a rain-cloud, a male lightning-bringer.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/226.]]

That is: "and he is the rain-bringer."

*And indeed for you is a reward never cut off* (68:3): uncut and not diminished, from their saying: "a rope that is *manin*" when it is not strong.

*And indeed you are upon a magnificent character* (68:4). Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: a magnificent religion. Al-Hasan said: his character was the manners of the Qur'an. Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her), when she was asked about the character of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), said: "His character was the Qur'an."

Qatadah said: It is what he would enact of Allah's command and refrain from of Allah's prohibition. Junayd said: His character was called magnificent because he had no aspiration other than Allah.

Al-Wasiti said: Because he gave both worlds in exchange for the Truth. It was said: Because he associated with people through his character and detached from them in his heart, so his outward was with creation and his inward was with the Real. One of the sages advised a man, saying: "Hold to the truth with creation, and to sincerity with the Real."

It was said: Because he dedicated the world to Allah, exalted is He, as Allah commanded him by His saying: *Take what is easy of forgiveness* (7:199), and the rest of the verse. It was said: His character was made magnificent because He made the colours small in his eyes, so that he might know their Creator.

It was said: His character was called magnificent because the noble qualities were gathered in him, as is indicated by what

It was related to us by Abu al-Qayyim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad the exegete, who said: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Saffar related to us, who said: Ibn Abi al-Rima related to us, who said: al-Darawardi related to us, from Ibn Ajlan, from al-Qa'qa', from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was sent only to perfect noble character." [3] [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 10/192.]]

And he said: "My Lord disciplined me, and He made my discipline excellent." [4] [[al-Jami' al-Saghir: 1/51.]]

[5] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/64.]]

He said: And Ahmad ibn Abi al-Farabi related to us, who said: Mansur ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ayyub al-Razi related to us, who said: Abu al-Walid related to us, who said: Shu'bah related to us, from al-Qasim and Abu Qurrah, who said: I heard Ata al-Kaykharani, from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Nothing is heavier in the scale than good character." "Hold to good character, for good character is surely in Paradise, and beware of bad character, for bad character is surely in the Fire." [7] [[Majma' al-Bayan: 10/87.]]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 68, verses 1–4:

It is Meccan. It has fifty-two verses, three hundred words, and one thousand two hundred and fifty-six letters.

It was related to us by Muhammad ibn al-Qayyim, who said: Muhammad ibn Taha related to us, who said: Ibrahim ibn Shurayk related to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah related to us, who said: Salam ibn Sulaym related to us, who said: Harun ibn Kathir related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his son, from Abu Umamah ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites the surah *Nun, wal-Qalam* (68), Allah will grant him the reward of those whose character Allah has made good." [1] [[Majma' al-Bayan: 10/82.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

**Nun.** The reciters differed concerning it. Some made its *nun* clear (*izhar*), while others concealed it (*ikhfa'*). Ibn Abbas read *Ni* with a kasra on the nun, on the assumption that a particle of oath is elided before it. Isa ibn Umar read it with a fatha, on the assumption that a verb such as *a'nni* (or similar) is elided before it.

The commentators differed about its meaning. Mujahid, Muqatil, Murrah al-Hamdani, Ata al-Khurasani, al-Suddi and al-Kalbi said:

It is the fish (*hut*) that carries the earth. This is the report of Abu Zabyan from Ibn Abbas, who said: The first thing Allah created was the pen, and it ran by what was to be until the Day of Resurrection. Then He raised it and created water, and from it He created the heavens. Then He created the *nun* and spread the earth upon the back of the *nun*. The *nun* moved, and the earth shook, so it was steadied with mountains, for the mountains boast over the earth. Then Ibn Abbas recited: *Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe* [68:1].

They differed about its name. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: *Yahmut*. Abu al-Yaqzan, al-Waqidi and Abu Ka'b said: *Lawsa*.

Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: *Yalhut*. And the rajiz said:

*What is it with you, that I see you all silent?*
*By Allah, my Lord is the Creator of the Yalhut.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/224, where it reads "al-Bahmut".]]

The narrators said: When Allah, exalted is He, created the earth and split it open, He sent from beneath the Throne an angel. He descended to the earth until he entered beneath the seven earths, and placed them upon his shoulder: one of his hands in the east and the other in the west, outstretched and grasping the seven earths, until he held them firm. But there was no place of rest for his foot. So Allah, exalted is He, sent down from Paradise (*al-Firdaws*) a bull with forty thousand horns and forty thousand legs, and placed the resting place of the angel's foot upon its hump. But his feet did not settle. So Allah caused a red ruby to descend from the highest rank of Paradise, whose thickness was a five-hundred-year journey, and placed it between the bull's hump and its ear, and his feet settled upon it. The horns of that bull extend out to the edges of the earth, and its nostrils are in the sea. It breathes out one breath each day; when it breathes out, the sea rises, and when it draws in its breath, the sea recedes. But the bull's hooves had no place of rest. So Allah created a green rock, as thick as the seven heavens and the seven earths, and the bull's hooves settled upon it. This is the rock of which Luqman said to his son: *"It would be in a rock"* (31:16). But the rock had no place of rest, so Allah created a *nun*, which is the great fish, and placed the rock upon its back and along its side. The fish is upon the sea, the sea is upon the wind, the wind is upon the power, and the weight of the whole world with what is upon it rests on two letters from the Book of Allah, exalted is He. The Almighty said to it: "Be," and it was.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: Iblis penetrated to the fish upon whose back the whole earth rests, and whispered to it, saying: "Do you know what is upon your back, O Luwtiya, of nations, animals, trees, mountains and other things? If you shook them off, you would cast them all from your back." He said: Luwtiya resolved to do that, but Allah sent a creature which entered its nostril and reached its brain. The fish cried out to Allah because of it, so He permitted it, and it came out. Ka'b said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, it looks at it and it looks at it; if it intends anything of that, it returns to what it was.

Some of them said: It is the last letter of *al-Rahman* (the Most Gracious). This is the report of Ikrimah from Ibn Abbas, who said: *Alif Lam Mim*? No: *Ra, Ha, Mim, Nun*, the letters of *al-Rahman*, blessed and exalted is He, separated.

Al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: The *nun* is the inkwell (*diwah*). This is the report of Thabit al-Yamani from Ibn Abbas. The poet said concerning it:

*When longing drives me toward them,*
*the nun casts down tears that flow like pearls.*

Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah said: It is a tablet of light, and he traced it back to the Prophet (ﷺ). [[See Tafsir al-Tabari: 29/21.]]

Ibn Zayd said: It is an oath which Allah, exalted is He, swore by. Ibn Kaysan said: It is the opening of the surah. Ata said: It is the opening letter of His name *Nur* (Light), *Nasir* (Helper) and *Nasir* (Victor). [[In Tafsir al-Qurtubi (15/289): The *ha'* is the opening of His names *Hamid* (Praiseworthy), *Hannan* (Compassionate), *Halim* (Forbearing) and *Hakim* (Wise), and the *mim* is the opening of His names *Malik* (King), *Majid* (Glorious), *Mannan* (Bestower), *Mutakabbir* (Majestic) and *Musawwir* (Fashioner).]] Al-Qurazi said: Allah swore by His support of the believers, as is shown by His saying: *It was ever a duty upon Us to help the believers* (30:47).

Ja'far al-Sadiq said: It is a river in Paradise. [[Zad al-Masir: 8/65.]]

***Wal-Qalam* (By the pen).** It is the pen with which the Reminder (*al-Dhikr*) was written. It is a pen of light, which lies between the heaven and the earth. It is said: When Allah created the pen, and it was the first thing He created, He looked at it, and it split into two halves. Then He said: "Run." It said: "O Lord, with what shall I run?" He said: "With what is to be until the Day of Resurrection." So it ran upon the Preserved Tablet by that.

Ata said: I asked al-Walid ibn Ubadah ibn al-Samit: What was the will of your father when death came to him? He said: He called me and said: "My son, fear Allah, and know that you will not fear Allah, nor will you attain knowledge, until you believe in Allah alone, and in the decree, its good and its evil. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The first thing Allah created was the pen. He said to it: Write. It said: O Lord, what shall I write? He said: Write the knowledge [[In the source: the decree.]].' So the pen ran at that hour, with what is to be forever." [2] [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 9/3.]]

It is related that Ibn al-Zayyat entered upon one of the caliphs and found him sorrowful. He said to him: "Refresh me, O Ibn al-Zayyat." So he composed:

*O Allah, the decree is Yours, and the decree prevails,*
*and the writing was on the tablet.*
*Wait for relief and its causes,*
*for despair is the worst thing you have while in relief.* [[Sharh Nahj al-Balaghah by Ibn Abi al-Hadid: 5/165.]]

Did he mean by the pen the writing and script, by which Allah bestowed favour upon His servants when He taught them? That is as He said: *He taught by the pen* (96:4).

The sages and eloquent speakers have greatly described the pen and its benefit. So why would one wish to leave this book without reflecting upon its gems?

Ibn Haytham said: From the majesty of the pen is that no book was written for Allah except with it, and therefore Allah swore by it. It was said: Pens are the mounts of the intelligent and the messengers of the noble.

It was said: The pen is the greatest injustice. It was said: Eloquence is of two kinds: eloquence of the tongue and eloquence of the fingers. The excellence of the eloquence of the fingers is that what the pens fix remains through the days, while the eloquence of the tongue is effaced by the years.

One of the sages said: The affairs of religion and of the world are sustained by two things: the pen and the sword, and the sword is under the banner of knowledge. Their poet said concerning this:

*If the pen serves the sword, before which the necks have bowed*
*and before whose wariness the nations have submitted,*
*then death, and death cannot be overcome by anything,*
*it has always followed what the pen has run by.*

*Thus Allah decreed for the pens, since they were created,*
*that the swords have been their servants since they were sharpened.* [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/85.]]

And al-Sanawbari said:

*A pen of weak, hollow reed*
*is more effective than a long, spear-like javelin.*
*And of blades, when they appear, I meet them,*
*and of the Indian sword polished and burnished.* [[al-Murhaf: a thin blade (Lisan al-Arab 12/99).]]

*And more daring than the lion*
*that scorches hearts when it appears on the battlefield.*

Abu al-Qayyim al-Sadusi recited, saying: Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi recited to me, saying: Ibn Safwan recited to me, a verse of Abu Tammam on its meaning:

*A blow from a writer with his eloquence*
*is more effective and more far-reaching than a keen sword.*
*People, when they resolve on hostility toward an envier,*
*shed blood with the points of pens.*

And al-Buhturi said:

*People, when they sharpen pens in anger,*
*then draw from them the water of desires,*
*gain by them over their enemies, though they are many,*
*what they could not gain by the Mashrafi swords.*

Another said:

*The sword, in anger, its polish shines,*
*but it is no more effective against calamities than its pen.*

And Ibn al-Rumi said:

*In his hand is a pen, and you need no more than a pen,*
*a sufficient arrow, and enough of a hand wrapped in it.*
*By it he erases and affirms the sustenance of servants,*
*so destinies are nothing but what he writes and erases.*

He said: And one of them recited in its description:

*A mute who speaks with decisive words,*
*whose body is silent and hollow,*
*all of him speaks within its sheath,*
*and by its silence its speech is known.*

And another in its description:

*Its bones are thin after its head was full,*
*it wastes and its enemy grows strong when it is cut.*
*It is dark at the height of day, its tongue*
*understands one who speaks what is not heard.*

*Its nourishment, and the trees that grow in its poverty,*
*when they are cut, the mounts of the fingers are bewildered.*
*For it the weeping of lovers, and their color,*
*except that they weep black tears.*

Another:

*This is the first verse for the two following verses:*
*It is attached, its edge is wholly single,*
*it erases some creation or death,*
*by its walking it is a living serpent, and by its color a spirit,*
*and the crime of a lover and the characteristics of good things.* [[So it is in the manuscript.]]

His saying: *And what they inscribe* (68:1): they write. It may mean: "and what writes them," meaning the scribes (*al-Safarah*). It was said: They are the plural of *al-katabah* (scribes).

*You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman* (68:2) means: you are not a madman, since Allah has favoured you with prophethood. It was said: by the protection of your Lord. It was said: It is like saying, "You are not a madman, praise be to Allah." It was said: The meaning is "You are not a madman, and the blessing belongs to your Lord," like their saying: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You," meaning "and praise belongs to You." Labid said:

*I was left alone in the world, having lost my tribe,*
*and a beneficial neighbour at Arbad departed from me.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/226, concerning the verse.]]

That is: "and he is Arbad."

Al-Nabighah said:

*They did not deprive themselves of the goodness of food, and their mother*
*was overflowed upon you by a rain-cloud, a male lightning-bringer.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/226.]]

That is: "and he is the rain-bringer."

*And indeed for you is a reward never cut off* (68:3): uncut and not diminished, from their saying: "a rope that is *manin*" when it is not strong.

*And indeed you are upon a magnificent character* (68:4). Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: a magnificent religion. Al-Hasan said: his character was the manners of the Qur'an. Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her), when she was asked about the character of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), said: "His character was the Qur'an."

Qatadah said: It is what he would enact of Allah's command and refrain from of Allah's prohibition. Junayd said: His character was called magnificent because he had no aspiration other than Allah.

Al-Wasiti said: Because he gave both worlds in exchange for the Truth. It was said: Because he associated with people through his character and detached from them in his heart, so his outward was with creation and his inward was with the Real. One of the sages advised a man, saying: "Hold to the truth with creation, and to sincerity with the Real."

It was said: Because he dedicated the world to Allah, exalted is He, as Allah commanded him by His saying: *Take what is easy of forgiveness* (7:199), and the rest of the verse. It was said: His character was made magnificent because He made the colours small in his eyes, so that he might know their Creator.

The narrators said: When Allah, exalted is He, created the earth and split it open, He sent from beneath the Throne an angel. He descended to the earth until he entered beneath the seven earths, and placed them upon his shoulder: one of his hands in the east and the other in the west, outstretched and grasping the seven earths, until he held them firm. The fish is upon the sea, the sea is upon the wind, the wind is upon the power, and the weight of the whole world with what is upon it rests on two letters from the Book of Allah, exalted is He. *the nun casts down tears that flow like pearls.*

Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah said: It is a tablet of light, and he traced it back to the Prophet (ﷺ). [[See Tafsir al-Tabari: 29/21.]]

Ibn Zayd said: It is an oath which Allah, exalted is He, swore by. Ibn Kaysan said: It is the opening of the surah. Ata said: It is the opening letter of His name *Nur* (Light), *Nasir* (Helper) and *Nasir* (Victor). [[In Tafsir al-Qurtubi (15/289): The *ha'* is the opening of His names *Hamid* (Praiseworthy), *Hannan* (Compassionate), *Halim* (Forbearing) and *Hakim* (Wise), and the *mim* is the opening of His names *Malik* (King), *Majid* (Glorious), *Mannan* (Bestower), *Mutakabbir* (Majestic) and *Musawwir* (Fashioner).]] Al-Qurazi said: Allah swore by His support of the believers, as is shown by His saying: *It was ever a duty upon Us to help the believers* (30:47).

Ja'far al-Sadiq said: It is a river in Paradise. [[Zad al-Masir: 8/65.]]

***Wal-Qalam* (By the pen).** It is the pen with which the Reminder (*al-Dhikr*) was written. It is a pen of light, which lies between the heaven and the earth. It is said: When Allah created the pen, and it was the first thing He created, He looked at it, and it split into two halves. Then He said: "Run." It said: "O Lord, with what shall I run?" He said: "With what is to be until the Day of Resurrection." So it ran upon the Preserved Tablet by that.

Ata said: I asked al-Walid ibn Ubadah ibn al-Samit: What was the will of your father when death came to him? He said: He called me and said: "My son, fear Allah, and know that you will not fear Allah, nor will you attain knowledge, until you believe in Allah alone, and in the decree, its good and its evil. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The first thing Allah created was the pen. He said to it: Write. It said: O Lord, what shall I write? He said: Write the knowledge [[In the source: the decree.]].' So the pen ran at that hour, with what is to be forever." [2] [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 9/3.]]

It is related that Ibn al-Zayyat entered upon one of the caliphs and found him sorrowful. He said to him: "Refresh me, O Ibn al-Zayyat." So he composed:

*O Allah, the decree is Yours, and the decree prevails,*
*and the writing was on the tablet.*
*Wait for relief and its causes,*
*for despair is the worst thing you have while in relief.* [[Sharh Nahj al-Balaghah by Ibn Abi al-Hadid: 5/165.]]

Did he mean by the pen the writing and script, by which Allah bestowed favour upon His servants when He taught them? That is as He said: *He taught by the pen* (96:4).

The sages and eloquent speakers have greatly described the pen and its benefit. So why would one wish to leave this book without reflecting upon its gems?

Ibn Haytham said: From the majesty of the pen is that no book was written for Allah except with it, and therefore Allah swore by it. It was said: Pens are the mounts of the intelligent and the messengers of the noble.

It was said: The pen is the greatest injustice. It was said: Eloquence is of two kinds: eloquence of the tongue and eloquence of the fingers. The excellence of the eloquence of the fingers is that what the pens fix remains through the days, while the eloquence of the tongue is effaced by the years.

One of the sages said: The affairs of religion and of the world are sustained by two things: the pen and the sword, and the sword is under the banner of knowledge. Their poet said concerning this:

*If the pen serves the sword, before which the necks have bowed*
*and before whose wariness the nations have submitted,*
*then death, and death cannot be overcome by anything,*
*it has always followed what the pen has run by.*

*Thus Allah decreed for the pens, since they were created,*
*that the swords have been their servants since they were sharpened.* [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/85.]]

And al-Sanawbari said:

*A pen of weak, hollow reed*
*is more effective than a long, spear-like javelin.*
*And of blades, when they appear, I meet them,*
*and of the Indian sword polished and burnished.* [[al-Murhaf: a thin blade (Lisan al-Arab 12/99).]]

*And more daring than the lion*
*that scorches hearts when it appears on the battlefield.*

Abu al-Qayyim al-Sadusi recited, saying: Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi recited to me, saying: Ibn Safwan recited to me, a verse of Abu Tammam on its meaning:

*A blow from a writer with his eloquence*
*is more effective and more far-reaching than a keen sword.*
*People, when they resolve on hostility toward an envier,*
*shed blood with the points of pens.*

And al-Buhturi said:

*People, when they sharpen pens in anger,*
*then draw from them the water of desires,*
*gain by them over their enemies, though they are many,*
*what they could not gain by the Mashrafi swords.*

Another said:

*The sword, in anger, its polish shines,*
*but it is no more effective against calamities than its pen.*

And Ibn al-Rumi said:

*In his hand is a pen, and you need no more than a pen,*
*a sufficient arrow, and enough of a hand wrapped in it.*
*By it he erases and affirms the sustenance of servants,*
*so destinies are nothing but what he writes and erases.*

He said: And one of them recited in its description:

*A mute who speaks with decisive words,*
*whose body is silent and hollow,*
*all of him speaks within its sheath,*
*and by its silence its speech is known.*

And another in its description:

*Its bones are thin after its head was full,*
*it wastes and its enemy grows strong when it is cut.*
*It is dark at the height of day, its tongue*
*understands one who speaks what is not heard.*

*Its nourishment, and the trees that grow in its poverty,*
*when they are cut, the mounts of the fingers are bewildered.*
*For it the weeping of lovers, and their color,*
*except that they weep black tears.*

Another:

*This is the first verse for the two following verses:*
*It is attached, its edge is wholly single,*
*it erases some creation or death,*
*by its walking it is a living serpent, and by its color a spirit,*
*and the crime of a lover and the characteristics of good things.* [[So it is in the manuscript.]]

His saying: *And what they inscribe* (68:1): they write. It may mean: "and what writes them," meaning the scribes (*al-Safarah*). It was said: They are the plural of *al-katabah* (scribes).

*You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman* (68:2) means: you are not a madman, since Allah has favoured you with prophethood. It was said: by the protection of your Lord. It was said: It is like saying, "You are not a madman, praise be to Allah." It was said: The meaning is "You are not a madman, and the blessing belongs to your Lord," like their saying: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You," meaning "and praise belongs to You." Labid said:

*I was left alone in the world, having lost my tribe,*
*and a beneficial neighbour at Arbad departed from me.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/226, concerning the verse.]]

That is: "and he is Arbad."

Al-Nabighah said:

*They did not deprive themselves of the goodness of food, and their mother*
*was overflowed upon you by a rain-cloud, a male lightning-bringer.* [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/226.]]

That is: "and he is the rain-bringer."

*And indeed for you is a reward never cut off* (68:3): uncut and not diminished, from their saying: "a rope that is *manin*" when it is not strong.

*And indeed you are upon a magnificent character* (68:4). Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: a magnificent religion. Al-Hasan said: his character was the manners of the Qur'an. Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her), when she was asked about the character of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), said: "His character was the Qur'an."

Qatadah said: It is what he would enact of Allah's command and refrain from of Allah's prohibition. Junayd said: His character was called magnificent because he had no aspiration other than Allah.

Al-Wasiti said: Because he gave both worlds in exchange for the Truth. It was said: Because he associated with people through his character and detached from them in his heart, so his outward was with creation and his inward was with the Real. One of the sages advised a man, saying: "Hold to the truth with creation, and to sincerity with the Real."

It was said: Because he dedicated the world to Allah, exalted is He, as Allah commanded him by His saying: *Take what is easy of forgiveness* (7:199), and the rest of the verse. It was said: His character was made magnificent because He made the colours small in his eyes, so that he might know their Creator.

It was said: His character was called magnificent because the noble qualities were gathered in him, as is indicated by what

It was related to us by Abu al-Qayyim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad the exegete, who said: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Saffar related to us, who said: Ibn Abi al-Rima related to us, who said: al-Darawardi related to us, from Ibn Ajlan, from al-Qa'qa', from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was sent only to perfect noble character." [3] [[al-Sunan al-Kubra: 10/192.]]

And he said: "My Lord disciplined me, and He made my discipline excellent." [4] [[al-Jami' al-Saghir: 1/51.]]

It was related to us by Abu Amr Ahmad ibn Abi al-Farabi, grandfather of Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm, who said: Ibn Abd al-Hakam related to us, who said: My father and Shu'ayb related to us, and al-Layth related to us, from Umar ibn Abi Amr, from al-Muttalib ibn Abd Allah, from Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Indeed the believer attains by his good character the rank of one who stands in prayer at night and fasts by day." [5] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/64.]]

He said: And Ahmad ibn Abi al-Farabi related to us, who said: Mansur ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ayyub al-Razi related to us, who said: Abu al-Walid related to us, who said: Shu'bah related to us, from al-Qasim and Abu Qurrah, who said: I heard Ata al-Kaykharani, from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Nothing is heavier in the scale than good character." [6] [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/446.]]

It was related to us by Ahmad ibn al-Sari al-Arudi in Darb al-Hajib, who said: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far al-Amani related to us, who said: Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Amir al-Ta'i related to us, who said: My father related to me, who said: Ali ibn Musa al-Rida related to us, who said: My father Musa ibn Ja'far related to us, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah said:

"Hold to good character, for good character is surely in Paradise, and beware of bad character, for bad character is surely in the Fire." [7] [[Majma' al-Bayan: 10/87.]]

It was related to us by Ibn Fanjawayh, who said: Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanbah related to us, who said: Sam'an related to us, from Ibn al-Jarud, who said: Salih related to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Abu Uthman al-Yahri, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"The most beloved of you to Allah [[In the source: to me.]] are those of you with the best character, those who are gentle and easy to approach, who love and are loved. And the most hated of you to Allah are those who go about with tale-bearing, who sow discord between friends [[In the source: the beloved.]], who seek out the faults of the innocent." [8] [[al-Mu'jam al-Awsat: 7/350.]]

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 68, verses 5–15:**

﴿فَسَتُبْصِرُ﴾ meaning: you will see, O Muhammad. ﴿وَيُبْصِرُونَ﴾ meaning: and they will see, namely those who accused him of madness. ﴿بِأَيِّكُمُ الْمَفْتُونُ﴾ The exegetes (mufassirun) differed over the meaning and interpretation of this verse. Some said: its meaning is "which of you is the madman," and it is a verbal noun (masdar) in the pattern of the passive participle, as one says: "Mā li-fulānin majnūn, wa-ma'qūd, wa-ma'qūl," meaning "jaladah" (toughness), "'aqd" (resolve) and "'aql" (reason). The poet said:

*"Until, when they left for his bones no flesh, and for his heart no ma'qūl (reason)."*

That is, no reason. This is the meaning of the statement of al-Dahhak, and of the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

It was also said: the bā' (in bi-) is in the sense of fī (in), its meaning being: "You will see and they will see in which of the two groups the madman is: in your group, O Muhammad, or in theirs."

The mafsun (the one afflicted) is the madman whom Satan has afflicted. It was also said that its interpretation is: "which of you is the mafsun," and this is the meaning of the statement of Mujahid, that the mafsun is Satan.

Others said: its meaning is "which of you is the mafsun," and the bā' is extra (za'idah), as in the Exalted's saying: ﴿تَنْبُتُ بِالدُّهْنِ﴾ ("grows with oil") [al-Mu'minun: 20] and ﴿يَشْرَبُ بِها عِبادُ اللَّهِ﴾ ("from which the servants of God drink") [al-Insan: 6]. This is the view of Qatadah, al-Akhfash [and Abu 'Ubayd].

The rajiz (reciter of rajaz verse) said:

*"We are the sons of Ju'dah, the people of al-Falaj; we strike with the sword and hope for relief through it."*

﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ ضَلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ﴾ "Indeed your Lord knows best who has strayed from His way, and He knows best those who are guided."

﴿فَلا تُطِعِ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ "So do not obey the deniers," in what they called you to of their wretched religion. It was revealed concerning the polytheists of Quraysh when they called him to the religion of his forefathers.

﴿وَدُّوا لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ﴾ "They wish that you would compromise, and they would compromise." 'Atiyyah and al-Dahhak said: "that you would disbelieve, and they would disbelieve."

Ibn 'Abbas, through the narration of al-Walibi, said: "that you would be lenient, and they would be lenient." al-Kalbi said: "that you would soften toward them, and they would soften." al-Hasan said: "that you would flatter them in your religion, and they would flatter them in their religion." Zayd ibn Aslam said: "that you would be hypocritical and show-off, and they would be hypocritical." Aban ibn Taghlib said: "that you would show them affection, and they would show you affection." al-'Awfi said: "that you would lie, and they would lie." 'Awf, from al-Hasan: "that you would abandon part of your affair, and they would abandon part of their affair." Ibn Kaysan: "that you would draw close to them, and they would draw close to you."

﴿وَلا تُطِعْ كُلَّ حَلَّافٍ﴾ "And do not obey every oft-swearer," one who swears much by falsehood. It is said to mean al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. It was also said: al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth. It was also said: al-Akhnas ibn Shariq.

﴿مَهِينٍ﴾ "contemptible," weak and worthless.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "a liar," and this is "qarin" (close companion) of it, because a man lies only from the baseness of his own self in his own eyes. Qatadah said: "one who abounds in evil."

﴿هَمَّازٍ﴾ "a slanderer," one who backbites and devours the flesh of people. al-Hasan said: "he is one who disparages a side of the gathering," from the verse: ﴿همزة﴾ ("slanderer").

﴿مَشَّاءٍ بِنَمِيمٍ﴾ "a going about with calumny." Qatadah said: "he goes about with tale-bearing, spoiling relations between people."

﴿مَنَّاعٍ لِلْخَيْرِ﴾ "withholding from good." Ibn 'Abbas said: "that is, for Islam; he withholds his children and kin from Islam and says: 'If any one of you enters the religion of Muhammad, I will never benefit him with anything.'" Others said: "that is, stingy with wealth, grudging of it in what is due."

﴿مُعْتَدٍ﴾ "transgressor," violent, oppressive, wrongdoing. ﴿أَثِيمٍ﴾ "sinful," wicked.

﴿عُتُلٍّ﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "the 'utul is the ruthless, severe, hypocritical one." 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr said: "the 'utull is the glutton, the great drinker, the strong, the harsh one, who is placed on the scale and his hair does not weigh; he pushes the angel of those [in hell] seventy thousand pushes."

'Ali and al-Hasan said: "the 'utull is the vile of character, the bad of character."

Yaman said: "he is the coarse, the harsh, the base of companionship." Muqatil said: "the bulky." al-Kalbi said: "he is the one severe in his disbelief, and every severe one among the Arabs is 'utull, and its origin is from al-'atl, which is pushing with violence."

﴿بَعْدَ ذلِكَ﴾ "after that," that is, in addition to that. ﴿زَنِيمٍ﴾ is the illegitimate claimed one, whose lineage is attached to a people while he is not of them.

The poet said:

*"A zanim whom men claim as an addition, as the forelegs are added to the hide's width."*

Hassan ibn Thabit said:

*"You are a claimed one, attached among the family of Hashim, as the single arrow is attached behind the rider."*

Another said:

*"A zanim whose father is not known, the son of an adulteress, of base descent and baseness."*

Maruh al-Hamdani said: "His father only claimed him after eighteen years." This is the view of most of the exegetes.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "The zanim is the one who has no origin."

It was also said: he is the one who has a zunmah (a hanging flesh) like the zunmah of a sheep.

'Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "In this noble verse there is a description which was not recognised until it was said ﴿زَنِيمٍ﴾, and then it was recognised; he had a zunmah on his neck by which he was known." 'Ikrimah said: "the zanim is the one known [for his baseness], as the sheep is known by its zunmah." al-Sha'bi said: "He is the one who has a sign in [evil] by which he is known, as the sheep is known by its zunmah."

al-Qurtubi, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and ['Ikrimah] said: "He is the disbelieving mongrel, known for evil, the suspect."

al-Walibi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "The zanim: the wrongdoer."

Abu 'Abd Allah Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qatifi told us: 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal told us: my father told us: Waki' told us: 'Abd al-Hamid told us, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Ghanm, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the 'utull zanim, and he said: "He is the severe of character, the bloated, the glutton, the great drinker, the one who has the means of food and drink, the oppressor of people, wide of belly."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Qatifi told us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Razin al-'Uqayli told us: Safwan ibn Salih told us: al-Walid ibn Muslim told us: Abu Shayyah Ibrahim ibn 'Uthman told me, from 'Uthman ibn 'Umayr, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Saddad ibn Aws, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No jawwaz, no ja'ẓari, no 'utull, and no zanim will enter Paradise." I said: "What is the jawwaz?" He said: "Every one who gathers and withholds." I said: "What is the ja'ẓari?" He said: "The coarse, the rough." I said: "What is the 'utull zanim?" He said: "Every one wide of belly, wide of throat, a great eater, a great drinker, violent, oppressive."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ibn Habash al-Muqri told us: Ibn Zanjawayh told us: Salamah told us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding His saying ﴿زَنِيمٍ﴾, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The sky weeps over a man whom Allah has made physically sound, whose belly He has made wide, and to whom He gave of the world a little (in the source, some), and so he was oppressive to people; that is the 'utull zanim." He said: "And the sky weeps over the old adulterer, whom the earth can hardly bear."

al-Thumali narrated from Mujahid concerning the zanim: "He had six fingers on his hand; on each thumb he had an extra finger." Most scholars hold that the zanim is the wicked claimed one. Strange reports have come in this matter, and we mention some of them; and success is from Allah.

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muqri informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Bashir told us: Ibn Khawsa informed us: Ibn Khunayq informed us: Yusuf ibn Asbat told us, from Abu Isra'il al-Mala'i, from Fudayl ibn 'Umar al-Faqmi, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The child of adultery will not enter Paradise, nor his child, nor his child's child."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Bishr told us: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tawasi informed us: Abu Badr 'Abbad ibn al-Walid told us: Hayyan ibn Halak told us: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn 'Iyad, from 'Isa ibn Hittan, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the children of adultery will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection in the form of monkeys and pigs."

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qati'i told us: 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal told us: my father told us: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Razi told us: Salamah ibn al-Fadl told us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn 'Uthman, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Rafi', from Maymunah, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "My nation will remain in good as long as the child of adultery has not spread among them. When the child of adultery spreads among them, Allah the Exalted will soon overtake them all with punishment."

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad informed us: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi told us: Ibrahim ibn al-Hasan al-Adami told us: Abu Umayyah Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tarsusi told us: Sa'id ibn Aws told us: Abu al-Ashhab (he is al-'Utaridi) said: I heard 'Ikrimah say: "When the children of adultery increase, the rain decreases."

﴿أَنْ كانَ ذا مالٍ وَبَنِينَ﴾ "because he possesses wealth and sons." Abu Ja'far, Ibn 'Amir and Ya'qub read ﴿آن﴾ with a long vowel (mad), and Abu Hatim chose this. Hamzah and 'Asim, in the narration of Abu Bakr, read ﴿أأن﴾ with two hamzahs, and others read it with a genitive (jarr).

As for the one who reads it as an interrogative, it has two meanings: the first, "Now that he possesses wealth and sons, when Our verses are recited to him, he says: 'Tales of the ancients.'" The second: "Now that he possesses wealth and sons, you obey him." As for the one who reads it as a statement, its meaning is: "So do not obey him, for he possessed [wealth and sons]."

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 68, verses 5–15:**

﴿فَسَتُبْصِرُ﴾ meaning: you will see, O Muhammad. ﴿وَيُبْصِرُونَ﴾ meaning: and they will see, namely those who accused him of madness. ﴿بِأَيِّكُمُ الْمَفْتُونُ﴾ The exegetes (mufassirun) differed over the meaning and interpretation of this verse. Some said: its meaning is "which of you is the madman," and it is a verbal noun (masdar) in the pattern of the passive participle, as one says: "Mā li-fulānin majnūn, wa-ma'qūd, wa-ma'qūl," meaning "jaladah" (toughness), "'aqd" (resolve) and "'aql" (reason). The poet said:

*"Until, when they left for his bones no flesh, and for his heart no ma'qūl (reason)."*

That is, no reason. This is the meaning of the statement of al-Dahhak, and of the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

It was also said: the bā' (in bi-) is in the sense of fī (in), its meaning being: "You will see and they will see in which of the two groups the madman is: in your group, O Muhammad, or in theirs."

The mafsun (the one afflicted) is the madman whom Satan has afflicted. It was also said that its interpretation is: "which of you is the mafsun," and this is the meaning of the statement of Mujahid, that the mafsun is Satan.

Others said: its meaning is "which of you is the mafsun," and the bā' is extra (za'idah), as in the Exalted's saying: ﴿تَنْبُتُ بِالدُّهْنِ﴾ ("grows with oil") [al-Mu'minun: 20] and ﴿يَشْرَبُ بِها عِبادُ اللَّهِ﴾ ("from which the servants of God drink") [al-Insan: 6]. This is the view of Qatadah, al-Akhfash [and Abu 'Ubayd].

The rajiz (reciter of rajaz verse) said:

﴿بَعْدَ ذلِكَ﴾ "after that," that is, in addition to that. ﴿زَنِيمٍ﴾ is the illegitimate claimed one, whose lineage is attached to a people while he is not of them.

The poet said:

*"A zanim whom men claim as an addition, as the forelegs are added to the hide's width."*

Hassan ibn Thabit said:

*"You are a claimed one, attached among the family of Hashim, as the single arrow is attached behind the rider."*

Another said:

*"A zanim whose father is not known, the son of an adulteress, of base descent and baseness."*

Maruh al-Hamdani said: "His father only claimed him after eighteen years." This is the view of most of the exegetes.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "The zanim is the one who has no origin."

It was also said: he is the one who has a zunmah (a hanging flesh) like the zunmah of a sheep.

'Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "In this noble verse there is a description which was not recognised until it was said ﴿زَنِيمٍ﴾, and then it was recognised; he had a zunmah on his neck by which he was known." 'Ikrimah said: "the zanim is the one known [for his baseness], as the sheep is known by its zunmah." al-Sha'bi said: "He is the one who has a sign in [evil] by which he is known, as the sheep is known by its zunmah."

al-Qurtubi, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and ['Ikrimah] said: "He is the disbelieving mongrel, known for evil, the suspect."

al-Walibi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "The zanim: the wrongdoer."

Abu 'Abd Allah Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Malik al-Qatifi told us: 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal told us: my father told us: Waki' told us: 'Abd al-Hamid told us, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Ghanm, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the 'utull zanim, and he said: "He is the severe of character, the bloated, the glutton, the great drinker, the one who has the means of food and drink, the oppressor of people, wide of belly."

I said: "What is the jawwaz?" He said: "Every one who gathers and withholds." I said: "What is the ja'ẓari?" He said: "The coarse, the rough." I said: "What is the 'utull zanim?" He said: "Every one wide of belly, wide of throat, a great eater, a great drinker, violent, oppressive."

﴿أَنْ كانَ ذا مالٍ وَبَنِينَ﴾ "because he possesses wealth and sons." Abu Ja'far, Ibn 'Amir and Ya'qub read ﴿آن﴾ with a long vowel (mad), and Abu Hatim chose this. Hamzah and 'Asim, in the narration of Abu Bakr, read ﴿أأن﴾ with two hamzahs, and others read it with a genitive (jarr).

As for the one who reads it as an interrogative, it has two meanings: the first, "Now that he possesses wealth and sons, when Our verses are recited to him, he says: 'Tales of the ancients.'" The second: "Now that he possesses wealth and sons, you obey him." As for the one who reads it as a statement, its meaning is: "So do not obey him, for he possessed [wealth and sons]."

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 68, verses 5–15:**

﴿فَسَتُبْصِرُ﴾ meaning: you will see, O Muhammad. ﴿وَيُبْصِرُونَ﴾ meaning: and they will see, namely those who accused him of madness. ﴿بِأَيِّكُمُ الْمَفْتُونُ﴾ The exegetes (mufassirun) differed over the meaning and interpretation of this verse. Some said: its meaning is "which of you is the madman," and it is a verbal noun (masdar) in the pattern of the passive participle, as one says: "Mā li-fulānin majnūn, wa-ma'qūd, wa-ma'qūl," meaning "jaladah" (toughness), "'aqd" (resolve) and "'aql" (reason). The poet said:

*"Until, when they left for his bones no flesh, and for his heart no ma'qūl (reason)."*

That is, no reason. This is the meaning of the statement of al-Dahhak, and of the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

It was also said: the bā' (in bi-) is in the sense of fī (in), its meaning being: "You will see and they will see in which of the two groups the madman is: in your group, O Muhammad, or in theirs."

The mafsun (the one afflicted) is the madman whom Satan has afflicted. It was also said that its interpretation is: "which of you is the mafsun," and this is the meaning of the statement of Mujahid, that the mafsun is Satan.

Others said: its meaning is "which of you is the mafsun," and the bā' is extra (za'idah), as in the Exalted's saying: ﴿تَنْبُتُ بِالدُّهْنِ﴾ ("grows with oil") [al-Mu'minun: 20] and ﴿يَشْرَبُ بِها عِبادُ اللَّهِ﴾ ("from which the servants of God drink") [al-Insan: 6]. This is the view of Qatadah, al-Akhfash [and Abu 'Ubayd].

The rajiz (reciter of rajaz verse) said:

*"We are the sons of Ju'dah, the people of al-Falaj; we strike with the sword and hope for relief through it."*

﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ ضَلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِينَ﴾ "Indeed your Lord knows best who has strayed from His way, and He knows best those who are guided."

﴿فَلا تُطِعِ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ "So do not obey the deniers," in what they called you to of their wretched religion. It was revealed concerning the polytheists of Quraysh when they called him to the religion of his forefathers.

﴿وَدُّوا لَوْ تُدْهِنُ فَيُدْهِنُونَ﴾ "They wish that you would compromise, and they would compromise." 'Atiyyah and al-Dahhak said: "that you would disbelieve, and they would disbelieve."

Ibn 'Abbas, through the narration of al-Walibi, said: "that you would be lenient, and they would be lenient." al-Kalbi said: "that you would soften toward them, and they would soften." al-Hasan said: "that you would flatter them in your religion, and they would flatter them in their religion." Zayd ibn Aslam said: "that you would be hypocritical and show-off, and they would be hypocritical." Aban ibn Taghlib said: "that you would show them affection, and they would show you affection." al-'Awfi said: "that you would lie, and they would lie." 'Awf, from al-Hasan: "that you would abandon part of your affair, and they would abandon part of their affair." Ibn Kaysan: "that you would draw close to them, and they would draw close to you."

﴿وَلا تُطِعْ كُلَّ حَلَّافٍ﴾ "And do not obey every oft-swearer," one who swears much by falsehood. It is said to mean al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. It was also said: al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth. It was also said: al-Akhnas ibn Shariq.

﴿مَهِينٍ﴾ "contemptible," weak and worthless.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "a liar," and this is "qarin" (close companion) of it, because a man lies only from the baseness of his own self in his own eyes. Qatadah said: "one who abounds in evil."

﴿هَمَّازٍ﴾ "a slanderer," one who backbites and devours the flesh of people. al-Hasan said: "he is one who disparages a side of the gathering," from the verse: ﴿همزة﴾ ("slanderer").

﴿مَشَّاءٍ بِنَمِيمٍ﴾ "a going about with calumny." Qatadah said: "he goes about with tale-bearing, spoiling relations between people."

﴿مَنَّاعٍ لِلْخَيْرِ﴾ "withholding from good." Ibn 'Abbas said: "that is, for Islam; he withholds his children and kin from Islam and says: 'If any one of you enters the religion of Muhammad, I will never benefit him with anything.'" Others said: "that is, stingy with wealth, grudging of it in what is due."

﴿مُعْتَدٍ﴾ "transgressor," violent, oppressive, wrongdoing. ﴿أَثِيمٍ﴾ "sinful," wicked.

﴿عُتُلٍّ﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "the 'utul is the ruthless, severe, hypocritical one." 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr said: "the 'utull is the glutton, the great drinker, the strong, the harsh one, who is placed on the scale and his hair does not weigh; he pushes the angel of those [in hell] seventy thousand pushes."

'Ali and al-Hasan said: "the 'utull is the vile of character, the bad of character."
