Al-Tha'labi (Commentary of al-Tha'alibi, *al-Jawahir al-Hisan*) on Surah 68, verses 16–41:

﴿We will brand him upon the snout﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "We will slash him with the sword, making it a lasting mark upon his nose." He said: "He fought on the day of Badr, and his nose was slashed with the sword in the fighting." (Tafsir al-Tabari: 29/35.) Qatadah said: "We will mark him with something." The Arabs say of a man who insults another with a lasting, ugly insult: "He has branded him with a brand of evil," meaning, "He has stuck to him a disgrace he will never leave, just as a brand does not fade and its mark does not wear away." Jarir said:

When I set my brand upon al-Farazdaq,
and upon al-Bu'aith (Khidash ibn Bishr, also said to be Bushair) I slit the nose of al-Akhtal.
(Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/237.)

He meant it as satire.

Abu al-'Aliyah and Mujahid said: "We will brand him upon his nose and blacken his face, and make for him a sign on the Day of Judgment by which the blackness of his face will be recognized." Al-Dahhak and al-Kisa'i said: "We will mark him upon his face." Huraiz ibn Muhammad ibn Jarir said:

"We will make his matter clear, a clear clarification, so that they will know him; nothing about him will remain hidden from them, just as the brand is not hidden upon the snouts."

Al-Farra' said: "Although the snout is specifically singled out for the brand, it is in the sense of the face, because a part of a thing is sometimes used to express the whole, and this principle has already passed."

Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: "Its meaning is: We will punish him for drinking wine. *Al-khurtum* means wine, and its plural is *kharatim*." A poet said:

You spend your day in amusement and mirth,
while at night you are a drinker of *kharatim*.
(Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/238.)

Allah's words: ﴿Indeed We have tested them﴾, meaning: We tested and examined the people of Makkah with famine and hunger. ﴿As We tested the companions of the garden﴾.

Abu 'Amr al-Farabi informed us: Abu Musa informed us: al-Hariri informed us: Faris ibn 'Umar informed us: Salih ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn Marwan informed us, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying, ﴿Indeed We have tested them as We tested the companions of the garden﴾: He said: "It was a garden in Yemen called al-Qayrawan, two farsakhs before San'a'. Travellers passed through it. It had been planted by a people from among the people of prayer. It belonged to a man who died, and his sons inherited it. Whenever the needy came when they harvested their palm-trees, whatever the sickle passed over and did not cut was for the needy. When something fell from above the sickle, it was left on the cloth (*bisat*), and whatever fell upon the cloth was also for the needy. When they reaped their crops, whatever the sickle passed over was for the needy, and when they threshed, whatever was scattered was theirs. When the father died, these brothers inherited it from their father. They said: 'By God, the wealth is little and the dependants are many. This practice was only carried out when the wealth was abundant and the dependants few. As for now, when the wealth is little and the dependants many, we cannot do this.' So they made an agreement among themselves one day to go out early before the people went out, to cut their palm-trees, and they did not make an exception—they did not say, 'If God wills.' So the people set out in the dark of night toward their garden to cut it, and they found it blackened, for a visitation (*ta'if*) of punishment from the night had struck it and burned it." ﴿So it became like the harvested﴾. That is His saying, ﴿When they swore﴾, meaning they swore, ﴿that they would surely cut it﴾, meaning, that they would harvest it and cut its fruit, ﴿in the morning﴾, meaning when they rose in the morning before the needy knew. ﴿And they did not make an exception﴾, meaning they did not say, "If God wills." ﴿Then a visitation from your Lord swept over it﴾, and a visitation is only at night. That visitation was a fire sent down from heaven, which burned it. ﴿While they were sleeping﴾. ﴿So it became like the harvested﴾, like the dark, black night. A poet said:

Your night has stretched out, black and dark,
and it does not part from a morning like *sarim*.
(Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/242.)

Al-Hasan said: "Good was cut off from it, so nothing remained in it." Ibn Kaysan said: "Like a black jar." Ibn Zayd said: "Like a land that has been harvested." Al-Akhfash said: "Like the morning that has been cut off from the night." Al-Marrawj said: "Like a sand-dune cut off from the main body of the sand." The root of *al-sarim* is *al-masrum* (the harvested); everything cut from something is *sarim*, so the night is *sarim* and the morning is *sarim*, because each of them is cut off from the other.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "Like black ash, in the dialect of Hudhaym."

﴿Then they called out to one another﴾, meaning some of them called to others, ﴿in the morning﴾, ﴿saying: Go early to your tilth, if you are going to harvest.﴾ ﴿So they set off﴾, meaning they went toward it, ﴿while they were whispering to one another﴾, meaning consulting, saying to each other: ﴿No needy person shall enter it today against you﴾. ﴿And they went early, with intent, able﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "With power, able in themselves." Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Hasan said: "With determination and effort." Al-Nakha'i, al-Qurtubi, Mujahid and 'Ikrimah said: "With a matter agreed upon among them that they had established." Ma'mar related from al-Hasan who said: "With poverty." It was also said: "With strength." Al-Suddi said: "*Al-harad* is the name of the garden." Sufyan said: "With rage and anger," and from this is the saying of al-Ashhab ibn Ramlah:

Black snakes met black hidden ones,
pouring out upon each other, with *harad*, the blood of the serpents.
(Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 29/40.)

There are two dialects for it: *harrad* and *harad*, like *al-darak* and *al-darak*. Abu 'Ubaydah and al-Qutabi said: "With prevention, and *al-harad* and *al-muharadah* mean prevention. The Arabs say: 'The year withheld rain (*haradat al-sanah*)' when there was no rain in it, and 'the she-camel withheld milk (*haradat al-naqah*)' when she had no milk."

A poet said:

When she withholds, or is dry,
she turns away from her hobbled leg (*tiniha*)...
(Lisan al-'Arab: 13/51, where it reads "fakka 'an," and Jami' al-Bayan: 29/40.)

It was also said: "With intent." The rajaz-poet said:

And a flood came, from God's command,
coming with the intent of the garden, which was flowing.
(Jami' al-Bayan: 29/41.)

Another said:

If I am angered, my anger is like a... a *mujriyya*,
a stout, quick one, dwelling in thickets, not to be approached.

and upon al-Bu'aith (Khidash ibn Bishr, also said to be Bushair) I slit the nose of al-Akhtal.

You spend your day in amusement and mirth,

(Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/238.)

Your night has stretched out, black and dark,
and it does not part from a morning like *sarim*.
(Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/242.)

Ibn 'Abbas said: "Like black ash, in the dialect of Hudhaym."

Black snakes met black hidden ones,
pouring out upon each other, with *harad*, the blood of the serpents.
(Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 29/40.)

(Lisan al-'Arab: 13/51, where it reads "fakka 'an," and Jami' al-Bayan: 29/40.)

And a flood came, from God's command,

(Jami' al-Bayan: 29/41.)

(Al-Sihah: 6/2301.)

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 68, verse 42–52:

﴿On the day when a shin will be laid bare﴾. That is, on a severe and dreadful matter, which is the arrival of the Hereafter. The common readers recited it with a dammed yā' (yukshafu), while Ibn 'Abbas read it with an open tā' (tukshafu), meaning that the Resurrection will uncover its shin. Al-Hasan read it with a dammed tā' (tukshafu) ﴿'an sāqin﴾, that is, on a severe and dreadful matter, which is the arrival of the Hereafter and the passing away of this world. This is a case of metaphor (isti'ārah). The Arabs say of a man who has fallen into a great matter that requires him to exert effort, struggle, and endure hardship: "He hitched up his shin (shammara 'an sāqihi)", so the shin is used in place of severity.

Durayd ibn al-Ṣimmah said, lamenting a man:

"Short of wrap, his lower leg showing,
Patient in exile, a climber of the heights."
[Lisān al-'Arab: 11/117.]

It is also said of a matter when it intensifies, grows grave, appears, and its blindness departs: "It uncovered its shin (kashafa 'an sāqihi)." This is permissible in the language even though the matter has no shin, just as one says: "The face of the matter brightened, and the opinion of the chest became straight." A poet describing a war said:

"It uncovered its shin for them,
and the plain evil appeared."
[Lisān al-'Arab: 10/168.]

Ibn 'Abbas recited:

"Be patient, 'Anāq, for it is an evil that remains;
your people have made the striking of necks customary for me."
[al-Durr al-Manthūr: 6/254.]

"The war has stood up among us on a shin."

Another said:

"She has uncovered her shin, so strike hard;
the war has come upon you, so be earnest."
[Fath al-Qadīr: 5/275.]

The Arabs say: "The war has uncovered its shin."

A poet said:

"I am amazed at myself, and at her solicitude,
and at the chasing of birds away from their provision."
[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/248.]

"In a year that has uncovered its shin,
red, stripping the flesh from its bones."
[al-'Irāq: with a dammed ʿayn, the bone without flesh; al-'Irq, with a fatha, is what contains flesh.]

Those concerned with interpretation said things similar to this.

Abū Bakr ibn 'Abd Aws informed us, Abū al-Ḥasan Maḥfūẓ informed us, 'Abd Allāh ibn Hāshim narrated to us, 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Sufyān, from 'Āṣim, from Sa'īd ibn Jubayr: ﴿On the day when a shin will be laid bare﴾, he said: "On the severity of the matter." Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is the most severe hour on the Day of Resurrection."

Al-Rabī' reported from al-'Aṭā': Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, Aḥmad ibn Ja'far ibn Salm al-Jatalī narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn 'Umar Ibn Mas'adah al-Bayrūtī narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn al-Wazīr al-Sulamī narrated to us, al-Walīd ibn Muslim narrated to us, Rawḥ ibn Junāḥ narrated to us, from the mawlā of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Azīz, from Abū Burdah, from Abū Mūsā al-Ash'arī, from the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿On the day when a shin will be laid bare﴾, he said: "A great light, before which they will fall down in prostration."[15] [Majma' al-Zawā'id: 7/128.]

Abū Muḥammad 'Abd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Rūmī informed us, reading to him in his mosque on Saturday, four days before the end of Dhū al-Ḥijjah in the year 386 AH, Abū al-'Abbās Muḥammad ibn Ishāq al-Sarrāj narrated to us, Zuhayr ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Mubārak narrated to us, Quraysh ibn Ḥayyān al-'Ijlī narrated to us, Bakr ibn Wā'il narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū 'Abd Allāh al-Agharr, from Abū Hurayrah who said: We said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?"

He said: "Do you suffer any harm from looking at the sun when there is no cloud beneath it?"

We said: "No."

He said: "Do you suffer any harm from looking at the moon on the night of the full moon?"

We said: "No."

He said: "Indeed you will see Him likewise. When the Day of Resurrection comes, the first and the last will be gathered, and a caller will call out: whoever used to worship anything, let him follow it. Their gods that they used to worship will be presented to them, and they will go and follow them until they throw them into the Fire. This community will remain, including its hypocrites, and it will be said to them: The people have gone and you remain. They will say: We have a Lord whom we have not seen yet. He will say: Would you recognise Him? They will say: Between us and Him there is a sign; when we see it we will recognise Him. Then a shin will be uncovered for them, and they will fall down in prostration before Him. Groups will remain whose backs are like the horns of cattle, wanting to prostrate, but they will not be able [to do so]."[16] [Jāmi' al-Bayān of al-Ṭabarī: 29/51, with variation.]

Imam Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm informed us, reading to him in Jumādā al-Ākhirah in the year 392 AH: Abū Bakr al-Shāfi'ī informed us, Abū Qilābah al-Raqqāshī narrated to us, Abū 'Āṣim al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Mukhlad narrated to us, Ismā'īl ibn Rāfi' narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazī, from a man of the Anṣār, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah the Exalted will take from the oppressor on behalf of the oppressed, until no injustice remains with anyone, to the point that he is required to separate milk mixed with water; then, when he has finished with that, a caller will call out, audible to all creatures: Let every people join their gods and what they used to worship besides Allah. No one who worshipped anything besides Allah will remain without his gods being displayed before him. Allah will make one of the angels in the form of 'Uzayr, and He will make one of the angels in the form of 'Īsā ibn Maryam. The Jews will follow this one, and the Christians will follow that one. Then the rest will follow them, and it is said: their gods will follow them into the Fire. These are the ones of whom Allah the Exalted says: ﴿If these were gods, they would not have entered it; and all of them will abide therein﴾ [Sūrat al-Anbiyā': 99]. When only the believers remain, among them the hypocrites, Allah will say to them: The people have gone, so join your gods and what you used to worship.

They will say: We have no god but Allah, and we did not worship other than Him. Allah the Exalted will then withdraw and remain for as long as He wills, then He will come to them and say: O people, the people have gone, so join your gods and what you used to worship. They will say: By Allah, we have no god but Allah, and we did not worship other than Him. Then a shin will be uncovered for them, and He will manifest to them of His greatness what they recognise as their Lord. They will fall down in prostration on their faces, and every hypocrite will fall on his back, for Allah will make their spines like the horns of cattle. Then the Bridge will be laid between the two sides of Hell."[17] [al-Durr al-Manthūr: 5/341, with variation.]

'Aqīl ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad informed us that Abū al-Faraj al-Baghdādī al-Qāḍī informed them, from Abū Ja'far al-Ṭabarī: Muḥammad ibn 'Abd Allāh ibn 'Abd al-Ḥakam narrated to us, my father and Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us from al-Layth, Khālid ibn Yazīd ibn Aslam narrated to us, from Abū Hilāl. Abū Ja'far said: Mūsā ibn 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Masrūqī also narrated to me, Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to us, Hishām ibn Sa'īd narrated to us, Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to us, from 'Aṭā' ibn Yasār, from Abū Sa'īd al-Khudrī who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, a caller will call out: Let every nation join what they used to worship (so the people of the cross will go with their cross, the people of idols with their idols, and the people of every god with their gods), and no one who used to worship an image, an idol, or a statue will remain, but they will all go until they fall into the Fire. There will remain those who worshipped Allah alone, pious and wicked, and remnants of the People of the Book. Then Hell will be brought, appearing like a mirage, its parts crushing one another. Then the Jews will be summoned and asked: What did you used to worship?

They will say: 'Uzayr the son of Allah. He will say: You have lied; Allah did not take a consort or a son. What then do you want? They will say: O our Lord, we are thirsty, give us to drink. He will say: Will you not come forward? They will go and fall into the Fire. Then the Christians will be summoned and asked: What did you used to worship?

They will say: The Messiah the son of Allah. He will say: You have lied; Allah did not take a consort or a son. What then do you want? They will say: O our Lord, we are thirsty, give us to drink. He will say: Will you not come forward? They will go and fall into the Fire. Those who worshipped Allah the Exalted, pious and wicked, will remain. Then Allah the Exalted, majestic is His majesty, will come to us in a form other than the form in which we saw Him the first time, and say: O people, every nation has joined what it worshipped, and we are waiting for our Lord whom we used to worship. He will say: I am your Lord. They will say: We seek refuge in Allah from You. He will say: Is there between you and Allah a sign that you recognise? They will say: Yes. Then a shin will be uncovered, and they will all fall down in prostration to Allah the Exalted. No one who had prostrated in the world for show, for reputation, or in hypocrisy will remain, but his back will become one solid plate; whenever he tries to prostrate, he falls on his back. Then He will take away our righteous and our sinners, and He will have returned to us in the form in which we saw Him the first time, and He will say: I am your Lord. They will say: Yes, You are our Lord, three times."[18] [Jāmi' al-Bayān of al-Ṭabarī: 29/50.]

Al-Ṭabarī also said, narrated by him: Abū Lahab narrated to us, Abū Bakr narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from al-Minhāl, from Qays ibn Bakr, who said: 'Abd Allāh told me, while he was with 'Umar: When the Day of Resurrection comes, people will stand before the Lord of the worlds for forty years, their eyes fixed on the sky, barefoot and naked, the sweat bridling them, and He will not speak to them for forty years. Then a caller will call out: O people, is it not just from your Lord, who created you, shaped you, and provided for you, then you worshipped other than Him, that each people should be given what they served? They will say: Yes. He will say: Then for every people what they used to worship besides Allah will be presented, and they will follow them until these throw them into the Fire. The Muslims and the hypocrites will remain, and it will be said: Will you not go? The people have gone. They will say: Until our Lord comes to us. He will say: Would you recognise Him?

They will say: If He acknowledges us. He will say: At that point a shin will be uncovered and He will manifest Himself to them, and whoever used to worship Him will fall down in prostration, while the hypocrites remain unable, as if there were rods in their backs. They will be taken to the Fire, and these will enter Paradise. This is His saying, glory be to Him and exalted: ﴿And they are called to prostration, but they are unable, with their eyes humbled; humiliation covers them﴾. That is because the believers raise their heads and faces, whiter than snow, while the faces of the disbelievers and hypocrites blacken. ﴿And they used to be called to prostration in the world while they were sound﴾, healthy, so they would not come and would refuse.

Ibrāhīm al-Taymī said: They were called to the obligatory prayer by the adhān and iqāmah, but they refused. Sa'īd ibn Jubayr said: They used to hear "Come to success (ḥayya 'alā al-falāḥ)" and would not come. Ka'b al-Aḥbār said: By Allah, this verse was revealed only concerning those who stay away from the congregations.

It is related that Rabī' ibn al-Jaythum was struck with paralysis, so he would walk between two men to the mosque. It was said to him: "O Abū Yazīd, if you sat, you would have a concession." He said: "Whoever hears 'Come to success', let him respond even if he must crawl."

It was said to Sa'īd ibn al-Musayyab: "Ṭāriq intends to kill you, so hide." He said: "Where Allah cannot decree over me?" It was said to him: "Then sit." He said: "I hear 'Come to success' and do not respond?"[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/251.]

﴿So leave Me with those who deny this discourse﴾, that is, leave Me and the deniers of this Qur'an. ﴿We will draw them on gradually from where they do not know﴾, that is, We will seize them, and they will be punished on the Day of Badr. It is also said: its meaning is that We will increase them in sorrow and abandonment, so they will increase in disobedience and transgression.

Sufyān al-Thawrī said: He will pour out blessings upon them and make them forget gratitude. Al-'Abbād (as in the manuscript) said: We do not punish them at the time of their disobedience so that they would awaken; rather We grant them respite and extend to them blessings until the thought of reflection departs from them, so they are favoured outwardly and drawn on in reality.

Al-Ḥasan said: How many a person is drawn on by kindness shown to him, how many a person is deceived by praise of him, and how many a person is deluded by being concealed.

﴿And I grant them respite; indeed My plan is firm﴾. ﴿Or do you ask them for a reward, so that they are burdened with debt?﴾ ﴿Or is the unseen with them, so that they write it down?﴾ ﴿So be patient for the judgement of your Lord, and do not be like the companion of the fish﴾, in hastiness, anger, and haste; this is Yūnus (ʿalayhi al-salām).

﴿When he called out while he was suppressed﴾, distressed. ﴿Had it not been that a blessing from his Lord overtook him﴾, that is, reached him, and in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh it is read as "tadārakatuhu" with a tā'; ﴿he would have been cast out onto the bare land while he was blameworthy﴾, reproached, sinful.

﴿But his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous﴾. ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost slip you with their eyes﴾. That is because the disbelievers wanted to harm the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and afflict him with the evil eye. A group of Quraysh looked at him and said: "We have never seen anyone like him, nor like his proofs."

It was also said: the evil eye was among the Banū Asad, so much so that a fat she-camel or a fat cow would pass by one of them, he would look at it and then say: "O girl, bring the measure and the dirham, and bring us meat from this cow," and it would not move before it fell dead and was slaughtered.

Al-Kalbī said: A man among the Arabs would remain without eating for two or three days, then lift the side of his tent, and camels would pass by him, and he would say: "I have never seen camels or sheep more beautiful than these," and before long a group and a number of them would fall. The disbelievers asked this man to strike the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with the evil eye and do to him the same, so he agreed and recited:

"Your people used to think you a lord,
and I suppose you are a lord who is struck by the eye."
[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 6/2171.]

Then Allah the Exalted protected His Prophet (ﷺ), and revealed: ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost slip you﴾, meaning: and those who disbelieve would almost.

﴿Would slip you﴾: the lām entered because of the presence of inna. Al-A'mash and ʿĪsā read "layurhiqūnaka" (would overwhelm you), which is the reading of Ibn 'Abbās and Ibn Mas'ūd, meaning: they would destroy you. The people of Madīnah read "layuzlaqūnaka" with an open yā', and others read it with a damma, and both are dialects, said: zallafahu yuzalliquhu zalqan, and azlaqahu yuzliquhu izlāqan, with one meaning. The commentators differed in their interpretation of it.

Ibn 'Abbās said: they would strike you with their eyes when they heard the Reminder.

It is said: "zahaqa al-sahm" and "zalaqa" when it passes through. Qatādah said, with the meaning of "yuzhiqūnaka" (would make you perish). Ma'mar from al-Kalbī: they would throw you down. Ḥayyān from him: they would turn you away from what you are upon of conveying the message. 'Aṭiyyah: they would hope for you. Al-Mu'arrikh: they would remove you. Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl and al-Akhfash: they would help you. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Yaḥyā said: they look at you with a sidelong glance, with fierce staring, by which they frighten you and show enmity towards you. Al-Suddī: they would strike you with their eyes. Ibn Zayd: they would touch you. Ja'far: they would devour you. Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Kaysān: they would kill you. This is like saying: "He struck me with his glance and killed me with his eye." A poet said:

"The slippery eyes strike you with their gaze,
and the arrows of the archer grow weary against you."

Another said:

"They exchange, when they meet in a place,
a glance that removes the footing of feet."
[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/256.]

Al-Ḥasan said: The remedy for the affliction of the evil eye is that a person recite this verse.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The evil eye is real; the eye enters a man into the grave, and a camel into the cooking pot." [19] [Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 9/226.]

﴿And they say: Indeed he is mad﴾, while he is not, meaning Muhammad; and it is said: the Qur'an. ﴿It is nothing but a Reminder to the worlds.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 68, verse 42–52:

﴿On the day when a shin will be laid bare﴾. That is, on a severe and dreadful matter, which is the arrival of the Hereafter. The common readers recited it with a dammed yā' (yukshafu), while Ibn 'Abbas read it with an open tā' (tukshafu), meaning that the Resurrection will uncover its shin. Al-Hasan read it with a dammed tā' (tukshafu) ﴿'an sāqin﴾, that is, on a severe and dreadful matter, which is the arrival of the Hereafter and the passing away of this world. This is a case of metaphor (isti'ārah). The Arabs say of a man who has fallen into a great matter that requires him to exert effort, struggle, and endure hardship: "He hitched up his shin (shammara 'an sāqihi)", so the shin is used in place of severity.

Durayd ibn al-Ṣimmah said, lamenting a man:

"Short of wrap, his lower leg showing,
Patient in exile, a climber of the heights."
[Lisān al-'Arab: 11/117.]

It is also said of a matter when it intensifies, grows grave, appears, and its blindness departs: "It uncovered its shin (kashafa 'an sāqihi)." This is permissible in the language even though the matter has no shin, just as one says: "The face of the matter brightened, and the opinion of the chest became straight." A poet describing a war said:

"It uncovered its shin for them,
and the plain evil appeared."
[Lisān al-'Arab: 10/168.]

Ibn 'Abbas recited:

"Be patient, 'Anāq, for it is an evil that remains;
your people have made the striking of necks customary for me."
[al-Durr al-Manthūr: 6/254.]

"The war has stood up among us on a shin."

Another said:

"She has uncovered her shin, so strike hard;
the war has come upon you, so be earnest."
[Fath al-Qadīr: 5/275.]

The Arabs say: "The war has uncovered its shin."

A poet said:

"I am amazed at myself, and at her solicitude,
and at the chasing of birds away from their provision."
[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/248.]

"In a year that has uncovered its shin,
red, stripping the flesh from its bones."
[al-'Irāq: with a dammed ʿayn, the bone without flesh; al-'Irq, with a fatha, is what contains flesh.]

Those concerned with interpretation said things similar to this.

Abū Bakr ibn 'Abd Aws informed us, Abū al-Ḥasan Maḥfūẓ informed us, 'Abd Allāh ibn Hāshim narrated to us, 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Sufyān, from 'Āṣim, from Sa'īd ibn Jubayr: ﴿On the day when a shin will be laid bare﴾, he said: "On the severity of the matter." Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is the most severe hour on the Day of Resurrection."

Al-Rabī' reported from al-'Aṭā': Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, Aḥmad ibn Ja'far ibn Salm al-Jatalī narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn 'Umar Ibn Mas'adah al-Bayrūtī narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn al-Wazīr al-Sulamī narrated to us, al-Walīd ibn Muslim narrated to us, Rawḥ ibn Junāḥ narrated to us, from the mawlā of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Azīz, from Abū Burdah, from Abū Mūsā al-Ash'arī, from the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿On the day when a shin will be laid bare﴾, he said: "A great light, before which they will fall down in prostration."[15] [Majma' al-Zawā'id: 7/128.]

Abū Muḥammad 'Abd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Rūmī informed us, reading to him in his mosque on Saturday, four days before the end of Dhū al-Ḥijjah in the year 386 AH, Abū al-'Abbās Muḥammad ibn Ishāq al-Sarrāj narrated to us, Zuhayr ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Mubārak narrated to us, Quraysh ibn Ḥayyān al-'Ijlī narrated to us, Bakr ibn Wā'il narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū 'Abd Allāh al-Agharr, from Abū Hurayrah who said: We said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?"

He said: "Do you suffer any harm from looking at the sun when there is no cloud beneath it?"

We said: "No."

He said: "Do you suffer any harm from looking at the moon on the night of the full moon?"

We said: "No."

He said: "Indeed you will see Him likewise. When the Day of Resurrection comes, the first and the last will be gathered, and a caller will call out: whoever used to worship anything, let him follow it. Their gods that they used to worship will be presented to them, and they will go and follow them until they throw them into the Fire. This community will remain, including its hypocrites, and it will be said to them: The people have gone and you remain. They will say: We have a Lord whom we have not seen yet. He will say: Would you recognise Him? They will say: Between us and Him there is a sign; when we see it we will recognise Him. Then a shin will be uncovered for them, and they will fall down in prostration before Him. Groups will remain whose backs are like the horns of cattle, wanting to prostrate, but they will not be able [to do so]."[16] [Jāmi' al-Bayān of al-Ṭabarī: 29/51, with variation.]

﴿And I grant them respite; indeed My plan is firm﴾. ﴿Or do you ask them for a reward, so that they are burdened with debt?﴾ ﴿Or is the unseen with them, so that they write it down?﴾ ﴿So be patient for the judgement of your Lord, and do not be like the companion of the fish﴾, in hastiness, anger, and haste; this is Yūnus (ʿalayhi al-salām).

﴿When he called out while he was suppressed﴾, distressed. ﴿Had it not been that a blessing from his Lord overtook him﴾, that is, reached him, and in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh it is read as "tadārakatuhu" with a tā'; ﴿he would have been cast out onto the bare land while he was blameworthy﴾, reproached, sinful.

﴿But his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous﴾. ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost slip you with their eyes﴾. That is because the disbelievers wanted to harm the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and afflict him with the evil eye. A group of Quraysh looked at him and said: "We have never seen anyone like him, nor like his proofs."

It was also said: the evil eye was among the Banū Asad, so much so that a fat she-camel or a fat cow would pass by one of them, he would look at it and then say: "O girl, bring the measure and the dirham, and bring us meat from this cow," and it would not move before it fell dead and was slaughtered.

Al-Kalbī said: A man among the Arabs would remain without eating for two or three days, then lift the side of his tent, and camels would pass by him, and he would say: "I have never seen camels or sheep more beautiful than these," and before long a group and a number of them would fall. The disbelievers asked this man to strike the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with the evil eye and do to him the same, so he agreed and recited:

"Your people used to think you a lord,
and I suppose you are a lord who is struck by the eye."
[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 6/2171.]

Then Allah the Exalted protected His Prophet (ﷺ), and revealed: ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost slip you﴾, meaning: and those who disbelieve would almost.

﴿Would slip you﴾: the lām entered because of the presence of inna. Al-A'mash and ʿĪsā read "layurhiqūnaka" (would overwhelm you), which is the reading of Ibn 'Abbās and Ibn Mas'ūd, meaning: they would destroy you. The people of Madīnah read "layuzlaqūnaka" with an open yā', and others read it with a damma, and both are dialects, said: zallafahu yuzalliquhu zalqan, and azlaqahu yuzliquhu izlāqan, with one meaning. The commentators differed in their interpretation of it.

Ibn 'Abbās said: they would strike you with their eyes when they heard the Reminder.

It is said: "zahaqa al-sahm" and "zalaqa" when it passes through. Qatādah said, with the meaning of "yuzhiqūnaka" (would make you perish). Ma'mar from al-Kalbī: they would throw you down. Ḥayyān from him: they would turn you away from what you are upon of conveying the message. 'Aṭiyyah: they would hope for you. Al-Mu'arrikh: they would remove you. Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl and al-Akhfash: they would help you. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Yaḥyā said: they look at you with a sidelong glance, with fierce staring, by which they frighten you and show enmity towards you. Al-Suddī: they would strike you with their eyes. Ibn Zayd: they would touch you. Ja'far: they would devour you. Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Kaysān: they would kill you. This is like saying: "He struck me with his glance and killed me with his eye." A poet said:

"The slippery eyes strike you with their gaze,
and the arrows of the archer grow weary against you."

Another said:

"They exchange, when they meet in a place,
a glance that removes the footing of feet."
[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/256.]

Al-Ḥasan said: The remedy for the affliction of the evil eye is that a person recite this verse.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The evil eye is real; the eye enters a man into the grave, and a camel into the cooking pot." [19] [Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 9/226.]

﴿And they say: Indeed he is mad﴾, while he is not, meaning Muhammad; and it is said: the Qur'an. ﴿It is nothing but a Reminder to the worlds.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 68, verse 42–52:

﴿On the day when a shin will be laid bare﴾. That is, on a severe and dreadful matter, which is the arrival of the Hereafter. The common readers recited it with a dammed yā' (yukshafu), while Ibn 'Abbas read it with an open tā' (tukshafu), meaning that the Resurrection will uncover its shin. Al-Hasan read it with a dammed tā' (tukshafu) ﴿'an sāqin﴾, that is, on a severe and dreadful matter, which is the arrival of the Hereafter and the passing away of this world. This is a case of metaphor (isti'ārah). The Arabs say of a man who has fallen into a great matter that requires him to exert effort, struggle, and endure hardship: "He hitched up his shin (shammara 'an sāqihi)", so the shin is used in place of severity.

Durayd ibn al-Ṣimmah said, lamenting a man:

"Short of wrap, his lower leg showing,
Patient in exile, a climber of the heights."
[Lisān al-'Arab: 11/117.]

It is also said of a matter when it intensifies, grows grave, appears, and its blindness departs: "It uncovered its shin (kashafa 'an sāqihi)." This is permissible in the language even though the matter has no shin, just as one says: "The face of the matter brightened, and the opinion of the chest became straight." A poet describing a war said:

"It uncovered its shin for them,
and the plain evil appeared."
[Lisān al-'Arab: 10/168.]

Ibn 'Abbas recited:

"Be patient, 'Anāq, for it is an evil that remains;
your people have made the striking of necks customary for me."
[al-Durr al-Manthūr: 6/254.]

"The war has stood up among us on a shin."

Another said:

"She has uncovered her shin, so strike hard;
the war has come upon you, so be earnest."
[Fath al-Qadīr: 5/275.]

The Arabs say: "The war has uncovered its shin."

A poet said:

"I am amazed at myself, and at her solicitude,
and at the chasing of birds away from their provision."
[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/248.]

"In a year that has uncovered its shin,
red, stripping the flesh from its bones."
[al-'Irāq: with a dammed ʿayn, the bone without flesh; al-'Irq, with a fatha, is what contains flesh.]

Those concerned with interpretation said things similar to this.

Abū Bakr ibn 'Abd Aws informed us, Abū al-Ḥasan Maḥfūẓ informed us, 'Abd Allāh ibn Hāshim narrated to us, 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Sufyān, from 'Āṣim, from Sa'īd ibn Jubayr: ﴿On the day when a shin will be laid bare﴾, he said: "On the severity of the matter." Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is the most severe hour on the Day of Resurrection."

Al-Rabī' reported from al-'Aṭā': Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, Aḥmad ibn Ja'far ibn Salm al-Jatalī narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn 'Umar Ibn Mas'adah al-Bayrūtī narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn al-Wazīr al-Sulamī narrated to us, al-Walīd ibn Muslim narrated to us, Rawḥ ibn Junāḥ narrated to us, from the mawlā of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Azīz, from Abū Burdah, from Abū Mūsā al-Ash'arī, from the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿On the day when a shin will be laid bare﴾, he said: "A great light, before which they will fall down in prostration."[15] [Majma' al-Zawā'id: 7/128.]

He said: "Do you suffer any harm from looking at the sun when there is no cloud beneath it?"

We said: "No."

He said: "Do you suffer any harm from looking at the moon on the night of the full moon?"

We said: "No."

He said: "Indeed you will see Him likewise. When the Day of Resurrection comes, the first and the last will be gathered, and a caller will call out: whoever used to worship anything, let him follow it. Their gods that they used to worship will be presented to them, and they will go and follow them until they throw them into the Fire. This community will remain, including its hypocrites, and it will be said to them: The people have gone and you remain. They will say: We have a Lord whom we have not seen yet. He will say: Would you recognise Him? They will say: Between us and Him there is a sign; when we see it we will recognise Him. Then a shin will be uncovered for them, and they will fall down in prostration before Him. Groups will remain whose backs are like the horns of cattle, wanting to prostrate, but they will not be able [to do so]."[16] [Jāmi' al-Bayān of al-Ṭabarī: 29/51, with variation.]

Imam Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm informed us, reading to him in Jumādā al-Ākhirah in the year 392 AH: Abū Bakr al-Shāfi'ī informed us, Abū Qilābah al-Raqqāshī narrated to us, Abū 'Āṣim al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Mukhlad narrated to us, Ismā'īl ibn Rāfi' narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazī, from a man of the Anṣār, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah the Exalted will take from the oppressor on behalf of the oppressed, until no injustice remains with anyone, to the point that he is required to separate milk mixed with water; then, when he has finished with that, a caller will call out, audible to all creatures: Let every people join their gods and what they used to worship besides Allah. No one who worshipped anything besides Allah will remain without his gods being displayed before him. Allah will make one of the angels in the form of 'Uzayr, and He will make one of the angels in the form of 'Īsā ibn Maryam. The Jews will follow this one, and the Christians will follow that one. Then the rest will follow them, and it is said: their gods will follow them into the Fire. These are the ones of whom Allah the Exalted says: ﴿If these were gods, they would not have entered it; and all of them will abide therein﴾ [Sūrat al-Anbiyā': 99]. When only the believers remain, among them the hypocrites, Allah will say to them: The people have gone, so join your gods and what you used to worship.

They will say: We have no god but Allah, and we did not worship other than Him. Allah the Exalted will then withdraw and remain for as long as He wills, then He will come to them and say: O people, the people have gone, so join your gods and what you used to worship. They will say: By Allah, we have no god but Allah, and we did not worship other than Him. Then a shin will be uncovered for them, and He will manifest to them of His greatness what they recognise as their Lord. They will fall down in prostration on their faces, and every hypocrite will fall on his back, for Allah will make their spines like the horns of cattle. Then the Bridge will be laid between the two sides of Hell."[17] [al-Durr al-Manthūr: 5/341, with variation.]

'Aqīl ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad informed us that Abū al-Faraj al-Baghdādī al-Qāḍī informed them, from Abū Ja'far al-Ṭabarī: Muḥammad ibn 'Abd Allāh ibn 'Abd al-Ḥakam narrated to us, my father and Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us from al-Layth, Khālid ibn Yazīd ibn Aslam narrated to us, from Abū Hilāl. There will remain those who worshipped Allah alone, pious and wicked, and remnants of the People of the Book. Then Hell will be brought, appearing like a mirage, its parts crushing one another. Then the Jews will be summoned and asked: What did you used to worship?

They will say: 'Uzayr the son of Allah. He will say: You have lied; Allah did not take a consort or a son. What then do you want? They will say: O our Lord, we are thirsty, give us to drink. He will say: Will you not come forward? They will go and fall into the Fire. Then the Christians will be summoned and asked: What did you used to worship?

They will say: The Messiah the son of Allah. He will say: You have lied; Allah did not take a consort or a son. What then do you want? They will say: O our Lord, we are thirsty, give us to drink. He will say: Will you not come forward? They will go and fall into the Fire. Those who worshipped Allah the Exalted, pious and wicked, will remain. Then Allah the Exalted, majestic is His majesty, will come to us in a form other than the form in which we saw Him the first time, and say: O people, every nation has joined what it worshipped, and we are waiting for our Lord whom we used to worship. He will say: I am your Lord. They will say: We seek refuge in Allah from You. He will say: Is there between you and Allah a sign that you recognise? They will say: Yes. Then a shin will be uncovered, and they will all fall down in prostration to Allah the Exalted. No one who had prostrated in the world for show, for reputation, or in hypocrisy will remain, but his back will become one solid plate; whenever he tries to prostrate, he falls on his back. Then He will take away our righteous and our sinners, and He will have returned to us in the form in which we saw Him the first time, and He will say: I am your Lord. They will say: Yes, You are our Lord, three times."[18] [Jāmi' al-Bayān of al-Ṭabarī: 29/50.]

Sa'īd ibn Jubayr said: They used to hear "Come to success (ḥayya 'alā al-falāḥ)" and would not come. He said: "Indeed you will see Him likewise. When the Day of Resurrection comes, the first and the last will be gathered, and a caller will call out: whoever used to worship anything, let him follow it. Their gods that they used to worship will be presented to them, and they will go and follow them until they throw them into the Fire. This community will remain, including its hypocrites, and it will be said to them: The people have gone and you remain. They will say: We have a Lord whom we have not seen yet. He will say: Would you recognise Him? They will say: Between us and Him there is a sign; when we see it we will recognise Him. Then a shin will be uncovered for them, and they will fall down in prostration before Him. Groups will remain whose backs are like the horns of cattle, wanting to prostrate, but they will not be able [to do so]."[16] [Jāmi' al-Bayān of al-Ṭabarī: 29/51, with variation.]

Imam Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm informed us, reading to him in Jumādā al-Ākhirah in the year 392 AH: Abū Bakr al-Shāfi'ī informed us, Abū Qilābah al-Raqqāshī narrated to us, Abū 'Āṣim al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Mukhlad narrated to us, Ismā'īl ibn Rāfi' narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazī, from a man of the Anṣār, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah the Exalted will take from the oppressor on behalf of the oppressed, until no injustice remains with anyone, to the point that he is required to separate milk mixed with water; then, when he has finished with that, a caller will call out, audible to all creatures: Let every people join their gods and what they used to worship besides Allah. No one who worshipped anything besides Allah will remain without his gods being displayed before him. Allah will make one of the angels in the form of 'Uzayr, and He will make one of the angels in the form of 'Īsā ibn Maryam. The Jews will follow this one, and the Christians will follow that one. Then the rest will follow them, and it is said: their gods will follow them into the Fire. These are the ones of whom Allah the Exalted says: ﴿If these were gods, they would not have entered it; and all of them will abide therein﴾ [Sūrat al-Anbiyā': 99]. When only the believers remain, among them the hypocrites, Allah will say to them: The people have gone, so join your gods and what you used to worship.

They will say: We have no god but Allah, and we did not worship other than Him. Allah the Exalted will then withdraw and remain for as long as He wills, then He will come to them and say: O people, the people have gone, so join your gods and what you used to worship. They will say: By Allah, we have no god but Allah, and we did not worship other than Him. Then a shin will be uncovered for them, and He will manifest to them of His greatness what they recognise as their Lord. They will fall down in prostration on their faces, and every hypocrite will fall on his back, for Allah will make their spines like the horns of cattle. Then the Bridge will be laid between the two sides of Hell."[17] [al-Durr al-Manthūr: 5/341, with variation.]

'Aqīl ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad informed us that Abū al-Faraj al-Baghdādī al-Qāḍī informed them, from Abū Ja'far al-Ṭabarī: Muḥammad ibn 'Abd Allāh ibn 'Abd al-Ḥakam narrated to us, my father and Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us from al-Layth, Khālid ibn Yazīd ibn Aslam narrated to us, from Abū Hilāl. Abū Ja'far said: Mūsā ibn 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Masrūqī also narrated to me, Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to us, Hishām ibn Sa'īd narrated to us, Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to us, from 'Aṭā' ibn Yasār, from Abū Sa'īd al-Khudrī who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, a caller will call out: Let every nation join what they used to worship (so the people of the cross will go with their cross, the people of idols with their idols, and the people of every god with their gods), and no one who used to worship an image, an idol, or a statue will remain, but they will all go until they fall into the Fire. There will remain those who worshipped Allah alone, pious and wicked, and remnants of the People of the Book. Then Hell will be brought, appearing like a mirage, its parts crushing one another. Then the Jews will be summoned and asked: What did you used to worship?

They will say: 'Uzayr the son of Allah. He will say: You have lied; Allah did not take a consort or a son. What then do you want? They will say: O our Lord, we are thirsty, give us to drink. He will say: Will you not come forward? They will go and fall into the Fire. Then the Christians will be summoned and asked: What did you used to worship?

They will say: The Messiah the son of Allah. He will say: You have lied; Allah did not take a consort or a son. What then do you want? They will say: O our Lord, we are thirsty, give us to drink. He will say: Will you not come forward? They will go and fall into the Fire. Those who worshipped Allah the Exalted, pious and wicked, will remain. Then Allah the Exalted, majestic is His majesty, will come to us in a form other than the form in which we saw Him the first time, and say: O people, every nation has joined what it worshipped, and we are waiting for our Lord whom we used to worship. He will say: I am your Lord. They will say: We seek refuge in Allah from You. He will say: Is there between you and Allah a sign that you recognise? They will say: Yes. Then a shin will be uncovered, and they will all fall down in prostration to Allah the Exalted. No one who had prostrated in the world for show, for reputation, or in hypocrisy will remain, but his back will become one solid plate; whenever he tries to prostrate, he falls on his back. Then He will take away our righteous and our sinners, and He will have returned to us in the form in which we saw Him the first time, and He will say: I am your Lord. They will say: Yes, You are our Lord, three times."[18] [Jāmi' al-Bayān of al-Ṭabarī: 29/50.]

Al-Ṭabarī also said, narrated by him: Abū Lahab narrated to us, Abū Bakr narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from al-Minhāl, from Qays ibn Bakr, who said: 'Abd Allāh told me, while he was with 'Umar: When the Day of Resurrection comes, people will stand before the Lord of the worlds for forty years, their eyes fixed on the sky, barefoot and naked, the sweat bridling them, and He will not speak to them for forty years. Then a caller will call out: O people, is it not just from your Lord, who created you, shaped you, and provided for you, then you worshipped other than Him, that each people should be given what they served? They will say: Yes. He will say: Then for every people what they used to worship besides Allah will be presented, and they will follow them until these throw them into the Fire. The Muslims and the hypocrites will remain, and it will be said: Will you not go? The people have gone. They will say: Until our Lord comes to us. He will say: Would you recognise Him?

They will say: If He acknowledges us. He will say: At that point a shin will be uncovered and He will manifest Himself to them, and whoever used to worship Him will fall down in prostration, while the hypocrites remain unable, as if there were rods in their backs. They will be taken to the Fire, and these will enter Paradise. This is His saying, glory be to Him and exalted: ﴿And they are called to prostration, but they are unable, with their eyes humbled; humiliation covers them﴾. That is because the believers raise their heads and faces, whiter than snow, while the faces of the disbelievers and hypocrites blacken. ﴿And they used to be called to prostration in the world while they were sound﴾, healthy, so they would not come and would refuse.

Ibrāhīm al-Taymī said: They were called to the obligatory prayer by the adhān and iqāmah, but they refused. Sa'īd ibn Jubayr said: They used to hear "Come to success (ḥayya 'alā al-falāḥ)" and would not come. Ka'b al-Aḥbār said: By Allah, this verse was revealed only concerning those who stay away from the congregations.

It is related that Rabī' ibn al-Jaythum was struck with paralysis, so he would walk between two men to the mosque. It was said to him: "O Abū Yazīd, if you sat, you would have a concession." He said: "Whoever hears 'Come to success', let him respond even if he must crawl."

It was said to Sa'īd ibn al-Musayyab: "Ṭāriq intends to kill you, so hide." He said: "Where Allah cannot decree over me?" It was said to him: "Then sit." He said: "I hear 'Come to success' and do not respond?"[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/251.]

﴿So leave Me with those who deny this discourse﴾, that is, leave Me and the deniers of this Qur'an. ﴿We will draw them on gradually from where they do not know﴾, that is, We will seize them, and they will be punished on the Day of Badr. It is also said: its meaning is that We will increase them in sorrow and abandonment, so they will increase in disobedience and transgression.

Sufyān al-Thawrī said: He will pour out blessings upon them and make them forget gratitude. Al-'Abbād (as in the manuscript) said: We do not punish them at the time of their disobedience so that they would awaken; rather We grant them respite and extend to them blessings until the thought of reflection departs from them, so they are favoured outwardly and drawn on in reality.

Al-Ḥasan said: How many a person is drawn on by kindness shown to him, how many a person is deceived by praise of him, and how many a person is deluded by being concealed.

﴿And I grant them respite; indeed My plan is firm﴾. ﴿Or do you ask them for a reward, so that they are burdened with debt?﴾ ﴿Or is the unseen with them, so that they write it down?﴾ ﴿So be patient for the judgement of your Lord, and do not be like the companion of the fish﴾, in hastiness, anger, and haste; this is Yūnus (ʿalayhi al-salām).

﴿When he called out while he was suppressed﴾, distressed. ﴿Had it not been that a blessing from his Lord overtook him﴾, that is, reached him, and in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh it is read as "tadārakatuhu" with a tā'; ﴿he would have been cast out onto the bare land while he was blameworthy﴾, reproached, sinful.

﴿But his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous﴾. ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost slip you with their eyes﴾. That is because the disbelievers wanted to harm the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and afflict him with the evil eye. A group of Quraysh looked at him and said: "We have never seen anyone like him, nor like his proofs."

It was also said: the evil eye was among the Banū Asad, so much so that a fat she-camel or a fat cow would pass by one of them, he would look at it and then say: "O girl, bring the measure and the dirham, and bring us meat from this cow," and it would not move before it fell dead and was slaughtered.

Al-Kalbī said: A man among the Arabs would remain without eating for two or three days, then lift the side of his tent, and camels would pass by him, and he would say: "I have never seen camels or sheep more beautiful than these," and before long a group and a number of them would fall. The disbelievers asked this man to strike the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with the evil eye and do to him the same, so he agreed and recited:

"Your people used to think you a lord,
and I suppose you are a lord who is struck by the eye."
[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 6/2171.]

Then Allah the Exalted protected His Prophet (ﷺ), and revealed: ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost slip you﴾, meaning: and those who disbelieve would almost.

﴿Would slip you﴾: the lām entered because of the presence of inna. Al-A'mash and ʿĪsā read "layurhiqūnaka" (would overwhelm you), which is the reading of Ibn 'Abbās and Ibn Mas'ūd, meaning: they would destroy you. The people of Madīnah read "layuzlaqūnaka" with an open yā', and others read it with a damma, and both are dialects, said: zallafahu yuzalliquhu zalqan, and azlaqahu yuzliquhu izlāqan, with one meaning. The commentators differed in their interpretation of it.

Ibn 'Abbās said: they would strike you with their eyes when they heard the Reminder.

It is said: "zahaqa al-sahm" and "zalaqa" when it passes through. Qatādah said, with the meaning of "yuzhiqūnaka" (would make you perish). Ma'mar from al-Kalbī: they would throw you down. Ḥayyān from him: they would turn you away from what you are upon of conveying the message. 'Aṭiyyah: they would hope for you. Al-Mu'arrikh: they would remove you. Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl and al-Akhfash: they would help you. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Yaḥyā said: they look at you with a sidelong glance, with fierce staring, by which they frighten you and show enmity towards you. Al-Suddī: they would strike you with their eyes. Ibn Zayd: they would touch you. Ja'far: they would devour you. Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Kaysān: they would kill you. This is like saying: "He struck me with his glance and killed me with his eye." A poet said:

"The slippery eyes strike you with their gaze,
and the arrows of the archer grow weary against you."

Another said:

"They exchange, when they meet in a place,
a glance that removes the footing of feet."
[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/256.]

Al-Ḥasan said: The remedy for the affliction of the evil eye is that a person recite this verse.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The evil eye is real; the eye enters a man into the grave, and a camel into the cooking pot." [19] [Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 9/226.]

﴿And they say: Indeed he is mad﴾, while he is not, meaning Muhammad; and it is said: the Qur'an. ﴿It is nothing but a Reminder to the worlds.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 68, verse 42–52:

﴿On the day when a shin will be laid bare﴾. That is, on a severe and dreadful matter, which is the arrival of the Hereafter. The common readers recited it with a dammed yā' (yukshafu), while Ibn 'Abbas read it with an open tā' (tukshafu), meaning that the Resurrection will uncover its shin. Al-Hasan read it with a dammed tā' (tukshafu) ﴿'an sāqin﴾, that is, on a severe and dreadful matter, which is the arrival of the Hereafter and the passing away of this world. This is a case of metaphor (isti'ārah). The Arabs say of a man who has fallen into a great matter that requires him to exert effort, struggle, and endure hardship: "He hitched up his shin (shammara 'an sāqihi)", so the shin is used in place of severity.

Durayd ibn al-Ṣimmah said, lamenting a man:

"Short of wrap, his lower leg showing,
Patient in exile, a climber of the heights."
[Lisān al-'Arab: 11/117.]

It is also said of a matter when it intensifies, grows grave, appears, and its blindness departs: "It uncovered its shin (kashafa 'an sāqihi)." This is permissible in the language even though the matter has no shin, just as one says: "The face of the matter brightened, and the opinion of the chest became straight." A poet describing a war said:

"It uncovered its shin for them,
and the plain evil appeared."
[Lisān al-'Arab: 10/168.]

Ibn 'Abbas recited:

"Be patient, 'Anāq, for it is an evil that remains;
your people have made the striking of necks customary for me."
[al-Durr al-Manthūr: 6/254.]

"The war has stood up among us on a shin."

Another said:

"She has uncovered her shin, so strike hard;
the war has come upon you, so be earnest."
[Fath al-Qadīr: 5/275.]

The Arabs say: "The war has uncovered its shin."

A poet said:

"I am amazed at myself, and at her solicitude,
and at the chasing of birds away from their provision."
[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/248.]

"In a year that has uncovered its shin,
red, stripping the flesh from its bones."
[al-'Irāq: with a dammed ʿayn, the bone without flesh; al-'Irq, with a fatha, is what contains flesh.]

Those concerned with interpretation said things similar to this.

Abū Bakr ibn 'Abd Aws informed us, Abū al-Ḥasan Maḥfūẓ informed us, 'Abd Allāh ibn Hāshim narrated to us, 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Sufyān, from 'Āṣim, from Sa'īd ibn Jubayr: ﴿On the day when a shin will be laid bare﴾, he said: "On the severity of the matter." Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is the most severe hour on the Day of Resurrection."

Al-Rabī' reported from al-'Aṭā': Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, Aḥmad ibn Ja'far ibn Salm al-Jatalī narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn 'Umar Ibn Mas'adah al-Bayrūtī narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn al-Wazīr al-Sulamī narrated to us, al-Walīd ibn Muslim narrated to us, Rawḥ ibn Junāḥ narrated to us, from the mawlā of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Azīz, from Abū Burdah, from Abū Mūsā al-Ash'arī, from the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿On the day when a shin will be laid bare﴾, he said: "A great light, before which they will fall down in prostration."[15] [Majma' al-Zawā'id: 7/128.]

Abū Muḥammad 'Abd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Rūmī informed us, reading to him in his mosque on Saturday, four days before the end of Dhū al-Ḥijjah in the year 386 AH, Abū al-'Abbās Muḥammad ibn Ishāq al-Sarrāj narrated to us, Zuhayr ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Mubārak narrated to us, Quraysh ibn Ḥayyān al-'Ijlī narrated to us, Bakr ibn Wā'il narrated to us, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū 'Abd Allāh al-Agharr, from Abū Hurayrah who said: We said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?"

He said: "Do you suffer any harm from looking at the sun when there is no cloud beneath it?"

We said: "No."

He said: "Do you suffer any harm from looking at the moon on the night of the full moon?"

We said: "No."

He said: "Indeed you will see Him likewise. When the Day of Resurrection comes, the first and the last will be gathered, and a caller will call out: whoever used to worship anything, let him follow it. Their gods that they used to worship will be presented to them, and they will go and follow them until they throw them into the Fire. This community will remain, including its hypocrites, and it will be said to them: The people have gone and you remain. They will say: We have a Lord whom we have not seen yet. He will say: Would you recognise Him? They will say: Between us and Him there is a sign; when we see it we will recognise Him. Then a shin will be uncovered for them, and they will fall down in prostration before Him. Groups will remain whose backs are like the horns of cattle, wanting to prostrate, but they will not be able [to do so]."[16] [Jāmi' al-Bayān of al-Ṭabarī: 29/51, with variation.]

﴿And I grant them respite; indeed My plan is firm﴾. ﴿Or do you ask them for a reward, so that they are burdened with debt?﴾ ﴿Or is the unseen with them, so that they write it down?﴾ ﴿So be patient for the judgement of your Lord, and do not be like the companion of the fish﴾, in hastiness, anger, and haste; this is Yūnus (ʿalayhi al-salām).

﴿When he called out while he was suppressed﴾, distressed. ﴿Had it not been that a blessing from his Lord overtook him﴾, that is, reached him, and in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh it is read as "tadārakatuhu" with a tā'; ﴿he would have been cast out onto the bare land while he was blameworthy﴾, reproached, sinful.

﴿But his Lord chose him and made him among the righteous﴾. ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost slip you with their eyes﴾. That is because the disbelievers wanted to harm the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and afflict him with the evil eye. A group of Quraysh looked at him and said: "We have never seen anyone like him, nor like his proofs."

It was also said: the evil eye was among the Banū Asad, so much so that a fat she-camel or a fat cow would pass by one of them, he would look at it and then say: "O girl, bring the measure and the dirham, and bring us meat from this cow," and it would not move before it fell dead and was slaughtered.

Al-Kalbī said: A man among the Arabs would remain without eating for two or three days, then lift the side of his tent, and camels would pass by him, and he would say: "I have never seen camels or sheep more beautiful than these," and before long a group and a number of them would fall. The disbelievers asked this man to strike the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with the evil eye and do to him the same, so he agreed and recited:

"Your people used to think you a lord,
and I suppose you are a lord who is struck by the eye."
[al-Ṣiḥāḥ: 6/2171.]

Then Allah the Exalted protected His Prophet (ﷺ), and revealed: ﴿And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost slip you﴾, meaning: and those who disbelieve would almost.

﴿Would slip you﴾: the lām entered because of the presence of inna. Al-A'mash and ʿĪsā read "layurhiqūnaka" (would overwhelm you), which is the reading of Ibn 'Abbās and Ibn Mas'ūd, meaning: they would destroy you. The people of Madīnah read "layuzlaqūnaka" with an open yā', and others read it with a damma, and both are dialects, said: zallafahu yuzalliquhu zalqan, and azlaqahu yuzliquhu izlāqan, with one meaning. The commentators differed in their interpretation of it.

Ibn 'Abbās said: they would strike you with their eyes when they heard the Reminder.

It is said: "zahaqa al-sahm" and "zalaqa" when it passes through. Qatādah said, with the meaning of "yuzhiqūnaka" (would make you perish). Ma'mar from al-Kalbī: they would throw you down. Ḥayyān from him: they would turn you away from what you are upon of conveying the message. 'Aṭiyyah: they would hope for you. Al-Mu'arrikh: they would remove you. Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl and al-Akhfash: they would help you. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Yaḥyā said: they look at you with a sidelong glance, with fierce staring, by which they frighten you and show enmity towards you. Al-Suddī: they would strike you with their eyes. Ibn Zayd: they would touch you. Ja'far: they would devour you. Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Kaysān: they would kill you. This is like saying: "He struck me with his glance and killed me with his eye." A poet said:

"The slippery eyes strike you with their gaze,
and the arrows of the archer grow weary against you."

Another said:

"They exchange, when they meet in a place,
a glance that removes the footing of feet."
[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/256.]

Al-Ḥasan said: The remedy for the affliction of the evil eye is that a person recite this verse.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The evil eye is real; the eye enters a man into the grave, and a camel into the cooking pot." [19] [Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 9/226.]

﴿And they say: Indeed he is mad﴾, while he is not, meaning Muhammad; and it is said: the Qur'an. ﴿It is nothing but a Reminder to the worlds.﴾

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 68, verse 42–52:

﴿On the day when a shin will be laid bare﴾. That is, on a severe and dreadful matter, which is the arrival of the Hereafter. The common readers recited it with a dammed yā' (yukshafu), while Ibn 'Abbas read it with an open tā' (tukshafu), meaning that the Resurrection will uncover its shin. Al-Hasan read it with a dammed tā' (tukshafu) ﴿'an sāqin﴾, that is, on a severe and dreadful matter, which is the arrival of the Hereafter and the passing away of this world. This is a case of metaphor (isti'ārah). The Arabs say of a man who has fallen into a great matter that requires him to exert effort, struggle, and endure hardship: "He hitched up his shin (shammara 'an sāqihi)", so the shin is used in place of severity.

Durayd ibn al-Ṣimmah said, lamenting a man:

"Short of wrap, his lower leg showing,
Patient in exile, a climber of the heights."
[Lisān al-'Arab: 11/117.]

It is also said of a matter when it intensifies, grows grave, appears, and its blindness departs: "It uncovered its shin (kashafa 'an sāqihi)." This is permissible in the language even though the matter has no shin, just as one says: "The face of the matter brightened, and the opinion of the chest became straight." A poet describing a war said:

"It uncovered its shin for them,
and the plain evil appeared."
[Lisān al-'Arab: 10/168.]

Ibn 'Abbas recited:

"Be patient, 'Anāq, for it is an evil that remains;
your people have made the striking of necks customary for me."
[al-Durr al-Manthūr: 6/254.]

"The war has stood up among us on a shin."

Another said:

"She has uncovered her shin, so strike hard;
the war has come upon you, so be earnest."
[Fath al-Qadīr: 5/275.]

The Arabs say: "The war has uncovered its shin."

A poet said:

"I am amazed at myself, and at her solicitude,
and at the chasing of birds away from their provision."
[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 18/248.]

"In a year that has uncovered its shin,
red, stripping the flesh from its bones."
[al-'Irāq: with a dammed ʿayn, the bone without flesh; al-'Irq, with a fatha, is what contains flesh.]

Those concerned with interpretation said things similar to this.

Abū Bakr ibn 'Abd Aws informed us, Abū al-Ḥasan Maḥfūẓ informed us, 'Abd Allāh ibn Hāshim narrated to us, 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, from Sufyān, from 'Āṣim, from Sa'īd ibn Jubayr: ﴿On the day when a shin will be laid bare﴾, he said: "On the severity of the matter." Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is the most severe hour on the Day of Resurrection."

Al-Rabī' reported from al-'Aṭā': Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, Aḥmad ibn Ja'far ibn Salm al-Jatalī narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn 'Umar Ibn Mas'adah al-Bayrūtī narrated to us, Muḥammad ibn al-Wazīr al-Sulamī narrated to us, al-Walīd ibn Muslim narrated to us, Rawḥ ibn Junāḥ narrated to us, from the mawlā of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Azīz, from Abū Burdah, from Abū Mūsā al-Ash'arī, from the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿On the day when a shin will be laid bare﴾, he said: "A great light, before which they will fall down in prostration."[15] [Majma' al-Zawā'id: 7/128.]

He said: "Do you suffer any harm from looking at the sun when there is no cloud beneath it?"

We said: "No."

He said: "Do you suffer any harm from looking at the moon on the night of the full moon?"

We said: "No."

He said: "Indeed you will see Him likewise. When the Day of Resurrection comes, the first and the last will be gathered, and a caller will call out: whoever used to worship anything, let him follow it. Their gods that they used to worship will be presented to them, and they will go and follow them until they throw them into the Fire. This community will remain, including its hypocrites, and it will be said to them: The people have gone and you remain. They will say: We have a Lord whom we have not seen yet. He will say: Would you recognise Him? They will say: Between us and Him there is a sign; when we see it we will recognise Him. Then a shin will be uncovered for them, and they will fall down in prostration before Him. Groups will remain whose backs are like the horns of cattle, wanting to prostrate, but they will not be able [to do so]."[16] [Jāmi' al-Bayān of al-Ṭabarī: 29/51, with variation.]

Imam Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm informed us, reading to him in Jumādā al-Ākhirah in the year 392 AH: Abū Bakr al-Shāfi'ī informed us, Abū Qilābah al-Raqqāshī narrated to us, Abū 'Āṣim al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Mukhlad narrated to us, Ismā'īl ibn Rāfi' narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazī, from a man of the Anṣār, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah the Exalted will take from the oppressor on behalf of the oppressed, until no injustice remains with anyone, to the point that he is required to separate milk mixed with water; then, when he has finished with that, a caller will call out, audible to all creatures: Let every people join their gods and what they used to worship besides Allah. No one who worshipped anything besides Allah will remain without his gods being displayed before him. Allah will make one of the angels in the form of 'Uzayr, and He will make one of the angels in the form of 'Īsā ibn Maryam. The Jews will follow this one, and the Christians will follow that one. Then the rest will follow them, and it is said: their gods will follow them into the Fire. These are the ones of whom Allah the Exalted says: ﴿If these were gods, they would not have entered it; and all of them will abide therein﴾ [Sūrat al-Anbiyā': 99]. When only the believers remain, among them the hypocrites, Allah will say to them: The people have gone, so join your gods and what you used to worship.

They will say: We have no god but Allah, and we did not worship other than Him. Allah the Exalted will then withdraw and remain for as long as He wills, then He will come to them and say: O people, the people have gone, so join your gods and what you used to worship. They will say: By Allah, we have no god but Allah, and we did not worship other than Him. Then a shin will be uncovered for them, and He will manifest to them of His greatness what they recognise as their Lord. They will fall down in prostration on their faces, and every hypocrite will fall on his back, for Allah will make their spines like the horns of cattle. Then the Bridge will be laid between the two sides of Hell."[17] [al-Durr al-Manthūr: 5/341, with variation.]

'Aqīl ibn Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad informed us that Abū al-Faraj al-Baghdādī al-Qāḍī informed them, from Abū Ja'far al-Ṭabarī: Muḥammad ibn 'Abd Allāh ibn 'Abd al-Ḥakam narrated to us, my father and Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us from al-Layth, Khālid ibn Yazīd ibn Aslam narrated to us, from Abū Hilāl. There will remain those who worshipped Allah alone, pious and wicked, and remnants of the People of the Book. Then Hell will be brought, appearing like a mirage, its parts crushing one another. Then the Jews will be summoned and asked: What did you used to worship?

They will say: 'Uzayr the son of Allah. He will say: You have lied; Allah did not take a consort or a son. What then do you want? They will say: O our Lord, we are thirsty, give us to drink. He will say: Will you not come forward? They will go and fall into the Fire. Then the Christians will be summoned and asked: What did you used to worship?

They will say: The Messiah the son of Allah. He will say: You have lied; Allah did not take a consort or a son. What then do you want? They will say: O our Lord, we are thirsty, give us to drink. He will say: Will you not come forward? They will go and fall into the Fire. Those who worshipped Allah the Exalted, pious and wicked, will remain. Then Allah the Exalted, majestic is His majesty, will come to us in a form other than the form in which we saw Him the first time, and say: O people, every nation has joined what it worshipped, and we are waiting for our Lord whom we used to worship. He will say: I am your Lord. They will say: We seek refuge in Allah from You. He will say: Is there between you and Allah a sign that you recognise? They will say: Yes. Then a shin will be uncovered, and they will all fall down in prostration to Allah the Exalted. No one who had prostrated in the world for show, for reputation, or in hypocrisy will remain, but his back will become one solid plate; whenever he tries to prostrate, he falls on his back. Then He will take away our righteous and our sinners, and He will have returned to us in the form in which we saw Him the first time, and He will say: I am your Lord. They will say: Yes, You are our Lord, three times."[18] [Jāmi' al-Bayān of al-Ṭabarī: 29/50.]

Sa'īd ibn Jubayr said: They used to hear "Come to success (ḥayya 'alā al-falāḥ)" and would not come.
